definition_zh: 独特的；有辨识度的；区别性的；特有的
definition_en: serving to distinguish something, or so characteristic that it is easily recognized
core_image: 一群相似的鸟里，有一只胸前的红斑独一无二
scene: 观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜，指向一只胸前有红斑的鸟。 On the birdwatching platform a group points through binoculars at a bird with a distinctive red patch on its breast.
sceneCN: 这里 distinctive 是「有辨识度的、独特的」（第 1 个义项：起区分作用的）；句意：观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜指向一只胸前有独特红斑的鸟。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、鸟群、胸前的红斑、图鉴。

pos.zh: 独特的；区别性的；有辨识度的

derivatives.zh: 清楚的；截然不同的
区别；优异；荣誉
独特地；醒目地
独特性；显著性

senses.title: Serving to tell one thing from another
senses.definition: marking a difference that allows one thing to be told apart from others
senses.definitionCN: 标示出某种差异，使一物能与别的区分开
senses.example: The distinctive feature of the species is its curved bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的显著特征是弯喙。
senses.why: Latin distinguere is dis- 'apart' plus stinguere 'to prick'. A distinctive mark is a pricked line that separates one thing from the next.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 distinguere 是 dis-“分开”加 stinguere“刺”。distinctive 的标记就是一条刺出来的线，把一物与下一物分开。

senses.title: Easy to recognize at once
senses.definition: so characteristic that it can be recognized quickly and confidently
senses.definitionCN: 特征明显到能被迅速且确信地认出
senses.example: She has a distinctive way of laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑起来的方式很有辨识度。
senses.why: Recognition is the practical test of a distinction. If the mark lets you pick the right one without hesitation, it is distinctive.
senses.whyCN: 认出是区分是否有效的实际检验。如果这个标记让你毫不犹豫地挑对，它就是有辨识度的。

senses.title: Belonging to one person or place
senses.definition: characteristic of a particular individual, group or region rather than of a whole class
senses.definitionCN: 属于特定个人、群体或地区而非整个类别的
senses.example: The valley has a distinctive microclimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷有独特的小气候。
senses.why: A distinction can be collective. The adjective then says that this feature belongs here and is not shared with neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 区分也可以是集体的。此时形容词表示这个特征属于此地，并不与邻处共享。

senses.title: A sound that changes meaning
senses.titleCN: 区别性语音特征（语言学）
senses.definition: in phonology, describing a sound feature that distinguishes one phoneme from another in a language
senses.definitionCN: 音系学中描述能在一门语言里把一个音位与另一个区分开的语音特征
senses.example: Voicing is a distinctive feature in English.
senses.exampleCN: 清浊对立在英语中是区别性特征。
senses.why: Phonology borrows the word for a formal job: if swapping the feature changes the word, the feature is distinctive; if not, it is not.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借这个词给一项形式化工作命名：若替换该特征会改变词义，它就是区别性的；若不会，就不是。

senses.title: A strength rivals cannot copy
senses.definition: in business strategy, describing a capability that sets a firm apart and is hard for rivals to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 战略管理中描述使公司与众不同且难以被对手模仿的能力
senses.example: Their distinctive competence is rapid prototyping.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的独特能力是快速原型开发。
senses.why: A firm survives by being separable from the crowd. Distinctive competence is the internal mark that makes the separation real rather than advertised.
senses.whyCN: 公司靠与众人可分开而存活。独特能力就是那个使分离成为真实而非广告说辞的内部标记。

senses.title: A mark that can be a trademark
senses.definition: in trademark law, describing a sign that consumers can use to identify the source of goods
senses.definitionCN: 商标法中描述消费者能借以识别商品来源的标志
senses.example: The court found the logo sufficiently distinctive.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该标识具有足够的显著性。
senses.why: A trademark must do the work of a distinction: tell this seller's goods from another's. Generic words cannot, so distinctiveness is a legal threshold.
senses.whyCN: 商标必须承担区分的工作：把这家的货与别家的分开。通用词做不到，因此显著性是法律门槛。

senses.title: Markings that identify an animal
senses.definition: in zoology, describing patterns or features by which individuals or species are identified
senses.definitionCN: 动物学中描述用于识别个体或物种的纹样或特征
senses.example: Each tiger has a distinctive stripe pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 每只老虎的条纹图案都独特。
senses.why: Nature supplies the marks that field guides rely on. The word moves from the observer's act of separating to the animal's visible equipment for being separated.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供了图鉴所依赖的标记。这个词从观察者的“分开”行为，转到动物身上“被分开”的可见装备。

senses.title: Having a character of its own
senses.definition: in design and criticism, describing a form that has a clear individual character rather than a generic one
senses.definitionCN: 设计与批评中描述具有清晰个体性格而非泛泛之形的形式
senses.example: The building has a distinctive silhouette.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑有独特的轮廓。
senses.why: Design aims at a shape you could pick out of a skyline. The adjective judges the result by the same test as sense 02: could you recognize it again?
senses.whyCN: 设计追求一个能从天际线里挑出来的形状。这个形容词用与第 2 义项相同的检验来评判结果：你能再认出它吗？

intro.en: Distinctive is distinct plus -ive. Distinct comes from Latin distinctus, the participle of distinguere, dis- 'apart' plus stinguere 'to prick'. The adjective marks whatever does the work of pricking out a difference.
intro.cn: distinctive 是 distinct 加 -ive。distinct 来自拉丁 distinctus，即 distinguere 的分词，由 dis-“分开”加 stinguere“刺”构成。这个形容词标记任何承担“刺出差异”这一工作的东西。

items.en: The root *steig- meant 'to prick, to stick'. It gives Latin stinguere and English stick, sting and stitch.
items.cn: 词根 *steig- 意为“刺、扎”。它给出拉丁 stinguere，以及英语 stick、sting、stitch。

items.en: Stinguere meant 'to prick, to extinguish'. With dis- it became distinguere, 'to separate by marking, to distinguish'. The image is a pointed tool drawing a line.
items.cn: stinguere 意为“刺、熄灭”。加 dis- 成为 distinguere“用标记分开、区分”。意象是一把尖工具划出一条线。

items.en: The participle distinctus meant 'separated, marked off'. The noun distinctio named a difference or a dividing. Both reached English through French.
items.cn: 分词 distinctus 意为“被分开、被标出”。名词 distinctio 指差异或划分。两者都经法语进入英语。

items.en: English distinct first means 'separate, individual', then 'clear to the senses'. The notion of clarity grows out of the notion of being marked off.
items.cn: 英语 distinct 初义为“分开的、个别的”，后指“感官上清晰的”。清晰这一观念正是从“被标出”生长出来的。

items.en: Distinctive appears in the 17th century as 'serving to distinguish'. It quickly extends to 'characteristic', since what distinguishes a thing is what we notice about it.
items.cn: distinctive 于 17 世纪出现，意为“起区分作用的”。它很快扩展到“有特征的”，因为使一物区别于他物的，正是我们注意到的东西。

items.en: Phonology adopts distinctive feature in the 1930s; trademark law and strategic management adopt distinctive character and distinctive competence later in the century.
items.cn: 音系学在 1930 年代采用 distinctive feature；商标法与战略管理在 20 世纪后半叶采用 distinctive character 与 distinctive competence。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the plain adjective, the noun of difference and the adverb. The meaning group contrasts distinctive with unique, characteristic and recognizable.
note.cn: 形近组区分普通形容词、表差异的名词与副词；词义组把 distinctive 与独特、典型、可辨认区分开。

entries.definition: clearly different or clearly perceived. It states separateness, while distinctive states the power to mark that separateness.
entries.definitionCN: 明显不同的，或明显可感的。它陈述分离，而 distinctive 陈述标记这种分离的能力。

entries.definition: a difference, or excellence. The adjective is built on the same participle.
entries.definitionCN: 差异，或优异。形容词由同一分词构成。

entries.definition: in a way that marks something out. It modifies the verb, while distinctive modifies the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以能标出某物的方式。它修饰动词，而 distinctive 修饰名词。

entries.definition: typical of a person or thing. It says the feature belongs to the type, while distinctive says it separates from the type.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某物所典型的。它说特征属于该类，而 distinctive 说特征使其脱离该类。

entries.definition: being the only one of its kind. It is absolute, while distinctive allows comparison and degree.
entries.definitionCN: 同类中唯一的。它是绝对的，而 distinctive 允许比较与程度。

entries.definition: able to be identified from previous experience. It describes the observer's success, not the feature's power.
entries.definitionCN: 能凭先前经验被认出的。它描述观察者的成功，而非特征的力量。

entries.definition: single, or having a personal style. It stresses separateness of being rather than the visible mark.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的，或有个人风格的。它强调存在的独立，而非可见的标记。

entries.definition: clearly noticeable. It measures strength of impression, while distinctive measures power to distinguish.
entries.definitionCN: 明显引人注意的。它衡量印象的强度，而 distinctive 衡量区分的能力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to a prick that draws a line, then follow that line into birds, voices, sounds, brands and buildings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词系在“刺出一条线”的动作上，再让这条线走到鸟、嗓音、语音、品牌与建筑。

normal.en: See stinguere, 'to prick': a distinctive mark is a line pricked out.
normal.cn: 看见 stinguere“刺”：distinctive 的标记就是刺出来的一条线。

normal.en: Test it by recognition: could you pick that bird out of a flock?
normal.cn: 用认出法检验：你能把那只鸟从鸟群里挑出来吗？

normal.en: For a voice, the mark is on the ear, not on the body.
normal.cn: 嗓音方面，标记在耳朵上，而不在身体上。

normal.en: In phonology, swap the feature: if the word changes, it is distinctive.
normal.cn: 音系学里，把特征换掉：若词变了，它就是区别性的。

normal.en: For trademarks, the test is source: can buyers tell whose goods these are?
normal.cn: 商标方面，检验是来源：买家能看出这是谁的货吗？

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one question: does this mark let you separate it from the rest?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个问题：这个标记能让你把它与其余的分开吗？

abstract.en: Notice that the word needs neighbours: nothing is distinctive in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词需要邻居：空房间里没有东西是独特的。

abstract.en: Keep the double role: the mark both separates and attracts attention.
abstract.cn: 记住双重角色：标记既分开，又吸引注意。

examples.en: The region is known for its distinctive architecture.
examples.cn: 这个地区以独特的建筑闻名。

examples.en: Stress is a distinctive feature in English word pairs.
examples.cn: 重音是英语词对中的一个区别性特征。

examples.en: The brand's distinctive logo is protected by law.
examples.cn: 该品牌独特的标识受法律保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯廷克提夫”：地斯廷克（distinct）一提，大家就认出是谁——distinctive 就是独特的、有辨识度的。

root: 拉丁语 stinguere“刺”，加 dis- 成 distinguere“用标记分开、区分”，分词 distinctus“被分开的”，加 -ive 构成 distinctive。同根词有 distinct、distinction、instinct、extinct、stimulus、stick、sting。

sensesIntro.en: Distinctive always answers one question: does this feature let you tell it apart? The feature may be a curved bill, a laugh, a valley's climate, a voiced consonant, a firm's capability, a logo, a tiger's stripes or a building's outline. The eight senses move across biology, language, law and design, but each describes the same power, the power to draw a line that holds.
sensesIntro.cn: distinctive 始终回答一个问题：这个特征能让你把它分开吗？这个特征可以是弯喙、笑声、山谷的气候、浊辅音、公司的能力、标识、虎纹或建筑的轮廓。八个义项走过生物学、语言、法律与设计，但每一个描述的都是同一种力量：画出一条站得住的线。

core.en: A mark that separates: the feature by which a thing is picked out.
core.cn: 起分开作用的标记：借以把某物挑出来的特征。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: a mark that separates and a mark that is recognized.
branches.cn: 知觉：起分开作用的标记，以及能被认出的标记。

branches.en: NATURE AND PLACE: features belonging to a region or an animal.
branches.cn: 自然与地方：属于某地区或某动物的特征。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: a sound feature that changes meaning.
branches.cn: 语言：能改变词义的语音特征。

branches.en: MARKET AND LAW: capability and legally protected distinctiveness.
branches.cn: 市场与法律：能力，以及受法律保护的显著性。

branches.en: DESIGN: a form with a character of its own.
branches.cn: 设计：有自身性格的形式。

intro.en: Distinctive is a participle plus -ive. The items show the stinguere family, where the same root produces words of pricking, of putting out and of being stirred.
intro.cn: distinctive 是分词加 -ive。下列条目展示 stinguere 词族，同一词根产生表示“刺”“熄灭”与“被激起”的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb, its participle and its noun. The idea of a pricked boundary is present in all three.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词、分词与名词。被刺出的边界这一观念在三者中都在。

items.meaningCN: 起区分作用的；有特征的

items.meaning: clearly different; clear to the senses
items.exampleCN: 出现了两个明确的群体。

items.example: Light is a stimulus for the eye.

items.structure: Old English sticca, from the same prick root
items.meaning: a thin piece of wood; to pierce or adhere
items.example: Stick the needle into the cloth.

latinEntries.meaning: to separate by marking; to distinguish

definition_zh: 减轻；缓和；缓解；使缓和
definition_en: to make damage, risk or hardship less severe, especially by taking action in advance
core_image: 洪水到来前，人在堤脚铺开一层缓冲石，浪头拍到堤面时被卸掉一半的力
scene: 工程开工前先改设计，把可能出现的沉降控制在可接受范围内。 Careful design can mitigate the risk of settlement.
sceneCN: 这里指提前降低风险程度（第 2 个义项：缓和冲击或风险）；句意为精心设计能缓和沉降风险。图中可辨识物件：堤脚铺开的缓冲石、拍上堤面的浪头、卸力后散开的水花。

pos.zh: 减轻；缓和；缓解

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「起缓和作用的」，法律中指减轻情节
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者」（少用）
由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「未减弱的；彻底的」

senses.title: To reduce harm
senses.definition: to lower the amount of harm that an event or action causes
senses.definitionCN: 降低某一事件或行为造成的损害量
senses.example: Early warning mitigated the damage from the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 提前预警减轻了洪水造成的损害。
senses.why: The root is mild, and making harm mild is the whole idea of the word.
senses.whyCN: 词根是「温和」，把伤害化温和就是这个词的全部意思。

senses.title: To lower a risk
senses.definition: to reduce the probability or severity of a future danger
senses.definitionCN: 降低未来危险发生的可能或严重程度
senses.example: Regular inspection mitigates the risk of failure.
senses.exampleCN: 定期检查降低了失效风险。
senses.why: Risk is a future weight, and mitigation is placed before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 风险是未来的重量，而缓解是在它到来之前先布置。

senses.title: To ease pressure or pain
senses.definition: to make a burden or a sensation less severe for those experiencing it
senses.definitionCN: 让承受者的负担或感受变得不那么严重
senses.example: Respite care mitigated the strain on the family.
senses.exampleCN: 喘息照护缓解了这个家庭的负担。
senses.why: This is the everyday use, where the mild root meets a person's experience.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常用法，温和的词根与人切身的感受相遇。

senses.title: To reduce a penalty
senses.definition: to lower the severity of a punishment or a legal liability
senses.definitionCN: 降低处罚或法律责任的严厉程度
senses.example: The court mitigated the sentence because of his cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到他的配合，法院减轻了判决。
senses.why: Law treats a penalty as a weight that may be reduced, hence mitigation in sentencing.
senses.whyCN: 法律把处罚当作可以减轻的重量，所以量刑中有「减轻」。

senses.title: To slow climate change
senses.definition: to reduce the rate or scale of a long-term environmental change
senses.definitionCN: 降低长期环境变化的速度或规模
senses.example: Cutting emissions mitigates but does not reverse warming.
senses.exampleCN: 减排能减缓变暖，却不能逆转它。
senses.why: Climate writing uses the verb for slowing a process, not for undoing it.
senses.whyCN: 气候写作把这个动词用于「放慢过程」，而不是「撤回结果」。

senses.title: To cut a loss or cost
senses.definition: to make the financial or material cost of an event smaller
senses.definitionCN: 降低某一事件在金钱或材料上的代价
senses.example: The reserve fund mitigated the loss from the cancelled order.
senses.exampleCN: 储备金减少了订单取消带来的损失。
senses.why: Losses are counted, and to mitigate is to bring the count down.
senses.whyCN: 损失是要计数的，而缓解就是把计数降下来。

senses.title: To soften a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute or a disagreement less sharp without settling it
senses.definitionCN: 使争端或分歧不那么尖锐，但不一定解决它
senses.example: A neutral chair mitigated the tension in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一位中立的主持人缓和了会上的紧张。
senses.why: Conflict is heat, and the word lowers it rather than putting it out.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是热度，这个词是降温而非灭火。

senses.title: To relieve symptoms
senses.definition: to make the signs of an illness less troublesome while the cause remains
senses.definitionCN: 在病因仍在的情况下，使疾病表现不那么难受
senses.example: The cream mitigates itching but does not treat the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药膏能减轻瘙痒，却不处理病因。
senses.why: Medicine separates relief from cure, and mitigation sits firmly on the relief side.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分缓解与治愈，而缓解稳稳站在「缓解」这一边。

intro.en: Mitigate comes from Latin mitigare, to soften or make mild, from mitis, mild. The second element is generally taken to be agere, to do, though the exact formation is debated.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 mitigare「使软、使温和」，出自 mitis「温和」；第二部分一般认为是 agere「做」，但确切构词方式有争议。

items.en: Mitis meant mild, soft or ripe, and it described both weather and temperament.
items.cn: 这个词意为温和、柔软或成熟，既形容天气也形容性情。

items.en: The verb meant to soften, soothe or appease, and it was used of anger, pain and harsh measures.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使软、安抚、平息，用于怒气、疼痛与严厉措施。

items.en: The tail of mitigare is generally explained as agere, to do, but the exact formation is debated, so its source is uncertain.
items.cn: 词尾一般解释为 agere「做」，但确切构词有争议，宜标为来源不确定。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century, first for tempering harshness and later for reducing harm.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪采用这个动词，先指使严厉变缓，后指减少损害。

items.en: Sentencing and climate policy both gave the verb fixed objects, penalty and emissions.
items.cn: 量刑与气候政策都给这个动词添了固定宾语：刑罚与排放。

items.en: The verb militate, to have force against, comes from miles, a soldier, and must not be confused with mitigate.
items.cn: militate「产生不利作用」出自 miles「士兵」，不可与这个词混淆。

note.en: The first group shares the mild stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of relief.
note.cn: 第一组与「mitigate」共享「温和」词干或只是形近；第二组是与「缓解」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for circumstances that reduce blame.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指减轻责任的（情节）。

entries.definition: Not softened at all, hence complete or absolute.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全未减弱的，引申为彻底的。

entries.definition: To work against something, from miles, a soldier; a classic confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生不利作用，出自「士兵」，是经典的易混词。

entries.definition: To intervene between parties, from medius, middle.
entries.definitionCN: 指居中调停，出自「中间」。

entries.definition: To lighten pain or hardship, often after the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻痛苦或困苦，多在事后。

entries.definition: To bring down an amount, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低数量，是宽泛中性的说法。

entries.definition: To make smaller in degree or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指在程度或数量上变小。

entries.definition: To soften the force of something by mixing or moderating.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过掺和或节制削弱力度。

entries.definition: To make something less difficult or painful.
entries.definitionCN: 指使不那么困难或痛苦。

entries.definition: To make less hard or less severe, the literal root picture.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变软或变缓，正是词根的字面画面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the mild root, the legal phrase mitigating circumstances, and the false twin militate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「温和」词根、法律短语「减轻情节」，以及易混的 militate。

normal.en: Mitis is mild, so mitigate is to take the edge off something harsh.
normal.cn: mitis 是「温和」，所以这个词就是把锋利的地方磨钝。

normal.en: Mitigation is what you do before the flood, not after it.
normal.cn: 缓解是在洪水到来之前做的，不是之后。

normal.en: Law speaks of mitigating circumstances that lower a penalty.
normal.cn: 法律说「减轻情节」，用来降低处罚。

normal.en: Militate looks similar but comes from soldier and means to work against.
normal.cn: militate 形似，却出自「士兵」，意为产生不利作用。

normal.en: Climate policy pairs mitigate with adapt: one slows the change, the other lives with it.
normal.cn: 气候政策把「减缓」与「适应」配对：一个放慢变化，一个与之共存。

abstract.en: To mitigate is to accept that the harm will arrive and decide how much of it to absorb.
abstract.cn: 缓解，就是承认伤害会来，然后决定吸收掉其中多少。

abstract.en: A cushion does not stop the blow; it lengthens the time over which the blow is felt.
abstract.cn: 缓冲垫并不挡住打击，它只是拉长感受这一击的时间。

abstract.en: Whatever cannot be removed can still be made mild, and the word lives in that remaining room.
abstract.cn: 去不掉的东西仍可变得温和，这个词就活在那点剩下的余地。

examples.en: Planting trees along the bank mitigated erosion after the floods.
examples.cn: 沿河岸植树减轻了洪水后的侵蚀。

examples.en: The team mitigated the risk by testing each joint twice.
examples.cn: 团队把每个接缝测了两遍，以降低风险。

examples.en: The ruling mitigated the fine because the firm reported early.
examples.cn: 由于该公司主动报告，裁决减轻了罚款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米提盖特」——堤脚先铺缓冲石，浪头拍到就卸一半：减轻、缓和

root: 拉丁语 mitis「温和」→ mitigare「使软、使缓和」；第二成分一般认为是 agere「做」，但确切构词有争议，构成成分来源不确定。英语十六世纪引入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take the edge off something: harm, risk, pressure, penalty, warming, loss, conflict and symptoms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在磨钝某个东西的锋边：损害、风险、压力、处罚、变暖、损失、冲突与症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: buffer stones are laid before the flood, and the wave spends half its force on them.
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水到来前先铺缓冲石，浪头把一半的力耗在石上。

branches.en: THE HARM IS CUT: damage or financial loss is counted lower than it would have been.
branches.cn: 损害被削：实际损害或金钱损失比原本更低。

branches.en: THE FUTURE IS CUSHIONED: a danger is made less likely or less severe before it arrives.
branches.cn: 未来被垫住：危险在到来之前就被降低可能或严重度。

branches.en: THE BURDEN IS LIGHTENED: strain and symptoms are made easier to carry.
branches.cn: 负担变轻：压力与症状变得较易承受。

branches.en: THE PENALTY IS SOFTENED: a punishment or liability loses part of its weight.
branches.cn: 处罚被软化：刑罚或责任卸去一部分重量。

branches.en: THE PROCESS IS SLOWED: warming or a dispute loses heat without being extinguished.
branches.cn: 过程被放慢：变暖或争端降了温，却没有被扑灭。

intro.en: Mitigate is a Latin verb whose stem is short but whose endings have produced a whole English family.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁动词，词干很短，但词尾在英语里长出了整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies mitis and mitigare; the second element of the verb is debated, so it is described rather than asserted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 mitis 与 mitigare；动词的第二成分有争议，因此只作描述，不作断言。

items.example: The adjective covered weather, fruit and temperament.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词涵盖天气、果实与性情。

items.example: The verb was used of anger and pain.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于怒气与疼痛。

items.example: It comes from soldier, not from mild.

senses.title: Relating to nutrition
senses.titleCN: 与营养有关：泛指这一领域
senses.definition: concerning nutrition as a process or a field, without naming a specific value
senses.definitionCN: 涉及营养这一过程或领域，但不指名具体的数值
senses.example: The clinic offers nutritional advice for young mothers.
senses.exampleCN: 该诊所为准妈妈提供营养建议。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun into a general adjective of relation, the same pattern as nation to national.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词变成表示关系的泛形容词，nation 变 national 也是同一模式。

senses.title: Nutritional value
senses.titleCN: 营养价值：食物所含养分的数量与质量
senses.definition: the amount and quality of nutrients a food provides per unit, often per serving or per hundred grams
senses.definitionCN: 食物每单位（常按份或每百克）提供的养分数量与质量
senses.example: Refining removes much of the grain's nutritional value.
senses.exampleCN: 精加工去掉了谷物的大部分营养价值。
senses.why: Value language lets nutrition be compared and priced, so the adjective attaches to a measurable quantity.
senses.whyCN: 用「价值」这一说法能让营养被比较与计价，因此这个形容词常附着于可测量的量。

senses.title: Nutritional deficiency
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏：某种养分长期不足
senses.definition: a state caused by too little of one or more nutrients over time, producing specific symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 长期缺乏一种或多种养分造成的状态，会产生特定症状
senses.example: Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional deficiency worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 缺铁是全世界最常见的营养缺乏。
senses.why: Medicine labels the cause rather than the symptom, so a disease such as anaemia is traced back to a nutritional deficiency.
senses.whyCN: 医学命名的是原因而非症状，因此贫血这类疾病会被追溯到营养缺乏。

senses.title: Nutritional status
senses.titleCN: 营养状况：个体整体的营养水平
senses.definition: the overall condition of a person's body as judged by weight, growth, blood markers and diet
senses.definitionCN: 通过体重、生长、血液指标与膳食判断的个人身体整体状况
senses.example: The survey mapped the nutritional status of schoolchildren.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查描绘了学龄儿童的营养状况。
senses.why: Public health needs one phrase for the combined result of many measurements, so 'status' is added to the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要用一个短语概括多项测量的综合结果，因此在形容词后加上 status。

senses.title: Nutritional supplements and therapy
senses.definition: products or treatments that supply nutrients missing from the diet or unavailable through eating
senses.definitionCN: 补充膳食中缺失、或因无法进食而不能获得的养分的产品或治疗
senses.example: She took a nutritional supplement during pregnancy.
senses.exampleCN: 她在孕期服用了一种营养补充剂。
senses.why: The adjective marks the purpose, separating a nutrient product from a drug with a different action.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标明用途，把营养产品与作用机制不同的药物区分开。

senses.title: Nutritional labelling
senses.titleCN: 营养标签标注：法规要求的成分披露
senses.definition: the regulated declaration of nutrient content on food packaging
senses.definitionCN: 法规要求在食品包装上披露养分含量
senses.example: Nutritional labelling made sugar content impossible to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 营养标签标注让糖含量无处隐藏。
senses.why: Regulators name the panel after the adjective, so the word appears on every packet as a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 监管者以这个形容词命名标签，因此它作为法律类别出现在每个包装上。

senses.title: Nutritional requirements
senses.titleCN: 营养需求：维持健康所需的量
senses.definition: the amounts of each nutrient needed daily for health, set by expert committees
senses.definitionCN: 专家委员会设定的、每日维持健康所需的各养分数量
senses.example: The feed was formulated to meet the birds' nutritional requirements.
senses.exampleCN: 饲料按禽类的营养需求配制。
senses.why: Once needs are quantified, they become requirements, and the adjective ties them to nutrition rather than to appetite.
senses.whyCN: 一旦需求被量化，它就成了「要求」，而这个形容词把它与营养而非食欲联系起来。

senses.title: Nutritional ecology
senses.titleCN: 营养生态学：食物质量如何影响动物
senses.definition: the study of how the nutrient content of food shapes the behaviour, health and distribution of animals
senses.definitionCN: 研究食物的养分含量如何塑造动物行为、健康与分布
senses.example: Nutritional ecology explains why deer choose young shoots.
senses.exampleCN: 营养生态学解释了鹿为何选择嫩枝。
senses.why: Ecology borrows the adjective to study food quality rather than mere quantity, giving it a research field of its own.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借这个形容词研究食物质量而非仅有数量，从而形成一个独立研究领域。

intro.en: Nutritional is nutrition plus the adjective ending -al, from Latin -alis. The noun itself comes from Latin nutritio.
intro.cn: nutritional 是 nutrition 加形容词词尾 -al，后者出自拉丁 -alis。名词本身则来自拉丁 nutritio。

items.en: Latin nutrire 'to nourish, to suckle' is the ultimate source, and it also gives nutrient, nourish and nurse.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养、哺乳」是最终来源，它也给出 nutrient、nourish 与 nurse。

items.en: The action noun nutritio 'a feeding, nourishment' supplied the French and English noun nutrition.
items.cn: 行动名词 nutritio「喂养、营养」提供了法语与英语的 nutrition。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis meant 'relating to' and became English -al, visible in national, natural and nutritional.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -alis 意为「与……有关」，变为英语 -al，可见于 national、natural 与 nutritional。

items.en: As nutrition became a science, English formed nutritional to describe values, deficiencies and requirements. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着营养成为一门科学，英语造出 nutritional 来描述价值、缺乏与需求。最早的确切年代存疑。

items.en: The adjective spread into food law and ecology, producing fixed terms such as nutritional labelling and nutritional ecology.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到食品法规与生态学，产生了营养标签标注、营养生态学等固定术语。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English use of nutritional is not securely dated, and it may have appeared independently in medical and agricultural writing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：nutritional 的英语首见年代没有可靠定论，它可能在医学与农业文献中各自独立出现。

note.en: The first group holds adjective and noun forms from the same family that are constantly interchanged; the second holds adjectives describing food quality.
note.cn: 第一组是同族但常被互换的形容词与名词形式；第二组是描述食物质量的形容词。

entries.definition: Means 'rich in nutrients' and praises the food. Nutritional merely labels the dimension, as in nutritional value.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「富含养分的」，带有对食物的称赞。nutritional 只是标明维度，如营养价值。

entries.definition: The noun for the process or the science. Nutritional is the adjective built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示过程或学科的名词。nutritional 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The countable substance, as in essential nutrients. Nutritional describes a property of a whole food.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的物质，如必需营养素。nutritional 描述整个食物的一种属性。

entries.definition: A near synonym meaning 'serving as nourishment', still used in animal science, as in nutritive value.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「起滋养作用的」近义词，仍用于动物科学，如营养价值。

entries.definition: Relating to the diet as a whole, as in dietary fibre. It frames intake, while nutritional frames nutrient content.
entries.definitionCN: 与整体膳食有关，如膳食纤维。它框定摄入，而 nutritional 框定养分含量。

entries.definition: Describes food or living that is good for health, often with a moral or traditional overtone that nutritional lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有益健康的食物或生活，常带道德或传统色彩，而 nutritional 没有这层意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nutrition + -al: relating to nutrition.
normal.cn: nutrition + -al：与营养有关的。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritionist, nutritionally, nutritious, nutrient and malnutrition.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrition、nutritionist、nutritionally、nutritious、nutrient、malnutrition。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: nutritional value, nutritional status, nutritional supplement, nutritional labelling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：营养价值、营养状况、营养补充剂、营养标签标注。

normal.en: nutritional labels a dimension; nutritious praises the food.
normal.cn: nutritional 标明维度，nutritious 称赞食物。

normal.en: Removing bran lowers flour's nutritional value, which is why wholemeal is preferred.
normal.cn: 去掉麸皮会降低面粉的营养价值，这也是全麦更受青睐的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a magnified label with a table of numbers and one row circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被放大的标签，上面一张数字表格，其中一行被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Picture two loaves side by side, one dark and dense, one pale and airy.
abstract.cn: 想象两条面包并排，一条深色紧实，一条浅色松软。

abstract.en: Picture a child's growth chart where the line flattens for a year and then climbs again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张儿童生长图，曲线平了一年，然后又向上走。

examples.en: Wholemeal bread has a higher nutritional value than white bread.
examples.cn: 全麦面包的营养价值高于白面包。

examples.en: The team assessed the children's nutritional status before the programme.
examples.cn: 项目开始前，团队评估了儿童的营养状况。

examples.en: Nutritional labelling is mandatory on most packaged foods.
examples.cn: 多数包装食品必须标注营养标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nutrition（营养）+ al（的）」——与营养有关的 → nutritional 营养的

root: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」→ nutritio → nutrition；加拉丁 -alis（英语 -al）→ nutritional。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show one adjective doing different jobs: framing a topic, pricing a food, naming a deficiency, describing a person, a product, a label, a requirement and a research field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示同一个形容词的不同职务：框定话题、给食物定价、命名缺乏、描述个人、产品、标签、需求与一个研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnified food label with one row circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：被放大的食品标签，其中一行被红笔圈出。

branches.en: GENERAL FRAME: -al simply says the topic is nutrition.
branches.cn: 泛框定：-al 只是说话题属于营养。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: value and requirements turn nutrients into numbers to compare and prescribe.
branches.cn: 计量：价值与需求把养分变成可比较、可规定的数字。

branches.en: CLINICAL PICTURE: a deficiency is named, and a person's overall state is assessed.
branches.cn: 临床图景：命名一种缺乏，并评估一个人的整体状态。

branches.en: REMEDY: supplements and therapy fill the gap that diet leaves.
branches.cn: 补救：补充剂与治疗填上膳食留下的缺口。

branches.en: LAW AND RESEARCH: labels are regulated, and ecology studies food quality.
branches.cn: 法规与研究：标签受监管，生态学研究食物质量。

intro.en: Nutritional is a Latin action noun with a Latin relational ending, so the whole word says 'pertaining to nourishment'.
intro.cn: nutritional 是拉丁行动名词加拉丁关系词尾，整个词的意思就是「与滋养相关的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin -alis gives English -al; the stem comes from nutritio, itself from nutrire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -alis 给出英语 -al；词干来自 nutritio，而 nutritio 又出自 nutrire。

items.example: The nutritional content varies with soil.
items.exampleCN: 营养成分随土壤而变化。

items.example: The meal was simple but nutritious.

definition_zh: 系统地；有条理地；按既定步骤逐一地

scene: 这里指「系统地」。 The team systematically checked every plot for signs of the disease.
sceneCN: 这里 systematically 指「系统地」（第 1 个义项：按既定方法一步一步执行）；句意：团队系统地检查了每一块样地有无该病害的迹象。图中可辨识物件：编号样方、记录板、逐格勾选的清单。

senses.title: By Fixed Method
senses.titleCN: 按既定方法：一步一步来
senses.definition: in a way that follows a fixed method or plan
senses.definitionCN: 按既定方法或计划地；有步骤地
senses.example: The samples were systematically labelled before any test began.
senses.exampleCN: 任何测试开始之前，样品都被系统地贴上了标签。
senses.why: Systematic work follows a system, that is, a set of steps kept in the same order each time. The adverb -ally says the action is carried out in exactly that order.
senses.whyCN: systematic 的工作遵循一个 system，也就是每次顺序相同的一套步骤；副词词尾 -ally 表示动作正是按这个顺序执行的。

senses.title: Covering Everything
senses.definition: in a way that covers every part of a set, leaving nothing out
senses.definitionCN: 全面地；无遗漏地覆盖每一部分
senses.example: She systematically searched every drawer for the missing key.
senses.exampleCN: 她把每个抽屉都系统地搜了一遍，寻找丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: If you go through all the members of a set in order, the set is covered. The word then carries the force of 'nothing skipped', which is why it pairs naturally with search, check and review.
senses.whyCN: 如果按顺序走遍一个集合的所有成员，这个集合就被覆盖了。此时该词带有「一处未漏」的力量，因此常与 search、check、review 搭配。

senses.title: As a Settled Policy
senses.titleCN: 一贯地：成体系地（常含贬义）
senses.definition: as a repeated, deliberate pattern, often with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 作为反复而蓄意的做法，常带批评语气
senses.example: The report was systematically ignored by the department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被该部门一贯地无视。
senses.why: A repeated pattern that looks planned rather than accidental is called systematic. The adverb then accuses someone of doing the same thing on purpose, again and again.
senses.whyCN: 一种看起来经过安排、而非偶然的重复模式，就叫 systematic；这个副词因此是在指责某人一次又一次地故意这么做。

senses.title: Across a Whole System
senses.titleCN: 从系统整体看：整体存在差异
senses.definition: with respect to a whole system rather than one of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 相对于整个系统而言，而非某个局部
senses.example: The two lakes differ systematically in depth and temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个湖在深度与温度上存在系统性的差异。
senses.why: Here the comparison is between whole systems. The difference is not a local accident but a property of each system taken together, so systematically marks the level of comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比较发生在两个完整系统之间：差异不是局部的偶然，而是各系统整体所具有的性质，因此 systematically 标出的是比较的层次。

senses.title: In Ordered Arrangement
senses.titleCN: 按体系排列：遵循分类秩序
senses.definition: in an ordered arrangement, especially one based on a classification
senses.definitionCN: 按有秩序的安排，尤指依据分类体系
senses.example: The specimens were systematically arranged by family.
senses.exampleCN: 标本按科系统地排列。
senses.why: A system can also be an order of classes or ranks. To arrange systematically is to follow that order rather than to place things by chance.
senses.whyCN: system 也可以指类别或等级的次序；按体系排列，就是遵循这个次序，而不是随手摆放。

senses.title: By Research Procedure
senses.titleCN: 按科研规程：系统综述与系统抽样
senses.definition: by the fixed procedures of systematic inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 按系统研究的固定规程
senses.example: The authors systematically reviewed forty trials before concluding.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在得出结论前系统地综述了四十项试验。
senses.why: Names such as systematic review and systematic sampling fix a procedure in advance. The adverb points to those procedures rather than to a general habit of tidiness.
senses.whyCN: systematic review、systematic sampling 这类名称事先就把规程固定下来；这个副词指向的是这些规程，而不只是一般的整齐习惯。

senses.title: According to a Prior Plan
senses.definition: according to a plan decided before the action
senses.definitionCN: 按照行动之前就已决定的计划
senses.example: They systematically cleared the site before the rain arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨来之前按计划清理了场地。
senses.why: When the steps are decided in advance, the doing follows the plan. The adverb marks that the plan, not the impulse of the moment, guided the work.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤事先定好，执行就是跟着计划走；这个副词标出的是计划——而不是一时冲动——在指挥这项工作。

senses.title: As a Regular Routine
senses.definition: in a regular, repeated routine
senses.definitionCN: 以有规律、反复的日常程序
senses.example: He systematically checks the gauges at the start of every shift.
senses.exampleCN: 每次上班开始时，他都按固定流程检查仪表。
senses.why: A routine repeats the same order each time, so it behaves like a small system. The adverb presents the habit as such a working order, neither accidental nor dramatic.
senses.whyCN: 日常程序每次都重复同一顺序，运行起来就像一个小系统；这个副词把该习惯呈现为这样一套工作秩序，既非偶然，也不夸张。

intro.en: Systematically is the adverb of systematic, which was built on system. System goes back through Latin systema to Greek systēma, a whole put together from parts. The date of the English adverb is given approximately.
intro.cn: systematically 是 systematic 的副词，而 systematic 建立在 system 之上。system 经拉丁 systema 上溯到希腊 systēma，指由各部分合成的一个整体。英语副词的首见年代为约数。

items.en: Greek syn- meant 'together' and histanai meant 'to make stand, to set up'. Combined they produced synistanai, 'to put together, to combine'. The root of histanai is the same *sta- that gives English stand and stable.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 syn- 意为「一起」，动词 histanai 意为「使立起、安置」。两者合成 synistanai，意为「组合、放在一起」。histanai 的词根与英语 stand、stable 同出 *sta-。

items.en: The noun systēma named an organized whole, whether a musical scale, a body of troops or a philosophical arrangement. The accent on 'organized' is already present in Greek.
items.cn: 名词 systēma 指有组织的整体，可以是一段音阶、一支部队，也可以是一套哲学安排。「有组织」这一重心在希腊语里就已存在。

items.en: Latin borrowed systema from Greek and used it mainly for a whole composed of parts. English took the word in the early seventeenth century, first in learned and theological writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 systema，主要用来指由部分组成的整体。英语于十七世纪初借入该词，最早见于学术与神学写作。

items.en: Systematic entered English in the seventeenth century from the Latinized Greek adjective systematicus. Adding -al + -ly produced systematically. The exact first citation is uncertain, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: systematic 于十七世纪经拉丁化的希腊形容词 systematicus 进入英语，再加 -al 与 -ly 构成 systematically。确切的首见书证不确定，故年代为约数。

items.en: Both adjectives derive from system but split in meaning. Systematic describes a method that follows ordered steps. Systemic describes a property of the whole system, as in systemic disease or systemic risk. The two are not interchangeable.
items.cn: 两个形容词都出自 system，但意义不同。systematic 描述遵循有序步骤的方法；systemic 描述整个系统的属性，如 systemic disease（全身性疾病）、systemic risk（系统性风险）。二者不可互换。

items.en: Modern statistics and evidence-based research fix phrases such as systematic error, systematic sampling and systematic review. In these names the adverb keeps its oldest force: the same procedure applied to every unit.
items.cn: 现代统计学与循证研究固定了 systematic error（系统误差）、systematic sampling（系统抽样）、systematic review（系统综述）等说法。在这些名称里，副词保留最古老的力量：同一套程序施加于每一个单位。

note.en: The first group separates two adjectives that both come from system but mean different things. The second group holds near-synonyms that stress order, procedure or repetition.
note.cn: 第一组区分两个都出自 system、但意义不同的形容词；第二组是强调秩序、程序或重复性的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a method that follows ordered steps. It answers the question 'how is the work done', not 'what does the whole consist of'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指遵循有序步骤的方法；回答的是「工作怎么做」，而不是「整体由什么构成」。

entries.definition: Describes something that affects or belongs to a whole system, such as the whole body or the whole economy. It is not a synonym of systematic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指影响或属于整个系统的，如整个身体或整个经济体；它并非 systematic 的同义词。

entries.definition: The adverb of systemic: 'in a way that affects the whole system'. It contrasts with systematically as whole-system does with methodical.
entries.definitionCN: systemic 的副词，意为「以影响整个系统的方式」；它与 systematically 的对立，正如「整体系统」与「讲究方法」的对立。

entries.definition: In an orderly way, following a method. It stresses calm sequence rather than complete coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 有条不紊地、按方法地；强调从容的顺序，而不强调覆盖全部。

entries.definition: In the same way on every occasion. It stresses repetition of a standard, not the internal order of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 每次都以同样方式地；强调标准的一致性，而非步骤的内部次序。

entries.definition: So thoroughly that nothing remains. It is stronger than systematically on coverage and says nothing about method.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底到不留余地地；在覆盖面上比 systematically 更强，但不涉及方法。

entries.definition: As an ordinary repeated practice. It stresses habit and frequency rather than designed procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 作为日常惯例地；强调习惯与频率，而非设计好的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: system + -atic + -ally: doing something as a small system of ordered steps.
normal.cn: system + -atic + -ally：把一件事当作一套有序步骤的小系统来做。

normal.en: The family runs system, systematic, systematically, systematize, systematics, systemic and subsystem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 system、systematic、systematically、systematize、systematics、systemic、subsystem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: systematic review, systematic sampling, systematic error, systematic search.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法义：系统综述、系统抽样、系统误差、系统搜索。

normal.en: systematic is about method; systemic is about the whole body or the whole system.
normal.cn: systematic 讲方法，systemic 讲整个身体或整个系统。

normal.en: A checklist is the everyday picture of this word: every line gets a tick in turn.
normal.cn: 清单是这个词的日常画面：每一行都依次被勾掉。

abstract.en: Picture a librarian walking every shelf from left to right, touching each spine once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位图书管理员从左到右走遍每一排书架，每一本书脊都碰一次。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that cannot skip a step, even when the step seems pointless.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器不会跳步，哪怕那一步看起来毫无必要。

abstract.en: Picture a pattern of footprints that repeats at exactly the same distance, so it must have been planned.
abstract.cn: 想象一串间距完全相同的脚印，因此它必然是事先安排好的。

examples.en: Before drawing conclusions, the researchers systematically coded every interview.
examples.cn: 在下结论之前，研究者把每一份访谈都系统地编码。

examples.en: The fault was not random: errors appeared systematically at low temperatures.
examples.cn: 这个故障并非随机：误差在低温下系统性出现。

examples.en: A government that systematically suppresses complaints will eventually lose its sources of information.
examples.cn: 一贯压制投诉的政府，最终会失去信息来源。

dict_mnemonic.text: system（系统）+ atic + ally（以……方式）→ 以系统的方式 → 系统地、有条理地

root: 希腊 syn-「一起」+ histanai「使立起」（*sta-「站立」）→ systēma「由部分组成的整体」→ 拉丁 systema → 英语 system → systematic → systematically。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one picture, a fixed order of steps, and apply it to different objects: a method, a complete coverage, a deliberate pattern, a whole system, a classification, a research procedure, a prior plan and a daily routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在同一幅画面上——一套固定的步骤次序——只是施加的对象不同：方法、全面覆盖、蓄意模式、整个系统、分类体系、科研规程、事先计划与日常流程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered steps in a fixed order, each box ticked in turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：按固定次序编号的步骤，每个格子依次被勾掉。

branches.en: METHOD AND COVERAGE: the same ordered path is used, and it is used until the set is finished.
branches.cn: 方法与覆盖：走同一条有序路径，并且走到整个集合完毕。

branches.en: INTENTION: when the same path recurs, observers stop calling it accidental and start calling it policy.
branches.cn: 意图：当同一条路径反复出现，旁观者就不再称之为偶然，而称之为既定做法。

branches.en: WHOLE AND ORDER: the system can be an entire object under comparison or a ranked scheme of classes.
branches.cn: 整体与秩序：system 既可以指被比较的完整对象，也可以指分等级的分类体系。

branches.en: PROTOCOL AND PLAN: research fixes the path in advance, and so does a plan made before the action.
branches.cn: 规程与计划：科研事先固定路径，行动之前订好的计划也是如此。

branches.en: ROUTINE: a habit that repeats the same order behaves like a small system running every day.
branches.cn: 日常流程：重复同一顺序的习惯，就像每天运行的一个小系统。

intro.en: Systematically is a Greek-derived noun turned adjective and then adverb: a prefix of union, a root of standing, an adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: systematically 是希腊来源的名词，先变形容词、再变副词：表示「结合」的前缀、表示「站立」的词根、形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Systema reached Latin from Greek and supplied system, systematic, systematize and systematics. Latin also has its own verb stare 'to stand', a cognate from the same Indo-European root rather than a source of the Greek word.
latinIntro.cn: systema 由希腊语进入拉丁语，衍生出 system、systematic、systematize、systematics。拉丁语本身另有动词 stare「站立」，它与希腊词同出同一个印欧词根，但并非希腊词的来源。

items.example: The files were systematically sorted by date.
items.exampleCN: 文件按日期系统地整理过。

items.example: The survey used a systematic sample of households.
items.exampleCN: 该调查使用了住户系统抽样。

items.structure: systema < Greek systēma (a whole put together)
items.example: The drainage system covers the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 排水系统覆盖整个山谷。

items.meaning: to reduce to an ordered system
items.example: She systematized the archive over one summer.
items.exampleCN: 她用一个夏天把档案系统化了。

items.meaning: the act of arranging into a system
items.example: The systematization of records took three years.
items.exampleCN: 档案的系统化用了三年。

items.meaning: the study of classification, especially of living things
items.meaningCN: 分类学，尤指生物分类学
items.example: Molecular systematics reshaped the tree of birds.
items.exampleCN: 分子分类学重塑了鸟类的演化树。

items.meaning: affecting the whole system or body
items.meaningCN: 影响整个系统或全身的
items.example: The infection became systemic within a week.
items.exampleCN: 感染在一周内变为全身性的。

items.meaning: a system contained within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 包含在更大系统内的子系统

latinEntries.structure: stare (verb, first conjugation); cognate with Greek histanai, not borrowed from it

definition_zh: 压缩；压紧；压力；压缩程度；数据压缩
definition_en: the act of pressing something so that it takes less space, the force produced by such pressing, or the reduction of data or content
core_image: 液压机把一块泡沫压到原来一半厚度，松手后它慢慢弹回一些
scene: 液压机把一块泡沫压到原来一半厚度，松手后它慢慢弹回一些。 The press applies compression until the foam halves in thickness.
sceneCN: 这里指把物体压小、压紧的动作（第 1 个义项：压缩动作）；句意为压机施加压缩，直到泡沫厚度减半。图中可辨识物件：压板、泡沫块、液压缸、压力表、厚度标尺。

pos.zh: 压缩；压力；压缩程度；数据压缩

derivatives.zh: 由该名词去掉名词词尾得到，义为「压缩；压紧」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「压缩机」
由该名词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「压缩的；抗压的」
由该动词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可压缩的」
由可压缩形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「可压缩性」

senses.title: The act of pressing down
senses.definition: the act of pressing or squeezing something so that it occupies less space
senses.definitionCN: 把某物压或挤，使其占据更小空间的动作
senses.example: Compression of the foam took only a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 泡沫的压缩只用了几秒钟。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to press together, and the noun simply names that pressing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「压到一起」，这个名词就直接指那种压。

senses.title: The force inside a solid
senses.definition: the internal force per unit area that pushes material together
senses.definitionCN: 使材料彼此靠拢的内部单位面积力
senses.example: The column fails when compression exceeds its strength.
senses.exampleCN: 当压力超过强度时，这根柱子会破坏。
senses.why: Engineers needed a word for the pushing side of force, and the pressing verb supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要一个词表示力的「推挤」一侧，表示压的动词正好提供。

senses.title: Shrinking a file
senses.definition: the reduction of the size of digital data by encoding it more efficiently
senses.definitionCN: 通过更高效的编码来减小数字数据体积
senses.example: Compression cut the image to a tenth of its size.
senses.exampleCN: 压缩把图像减到原来大小的十分之一。
senses.why: Digital files are treated as material that can be squeezed, and the metaphor is now the standard term.
senses.whyCN: 数字文件被当作可挤压的材料，这个比喻如今成了标准术语。

senses.title: The squeeze inside an engine
senses.definition: the reduction of the volume of a gas or fuel mixture in a cylinder before ignition
senses.definitionCN: 点火前气缸内气体或混合气体积的缩小
senses.example: A higher compression gives the engine more power.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的压缩程度使发动机功率更大。
senses.why: The piston literally compresses the charge, and the noun names both the stroke and its measure.
senses.whyCN: 活塞确实在压缩混合气，这个名词兼指冲程与其度量。

senses.title: Medical pressing
senses.definition: the application of steady pressure to a body part, as to stop bleeding
senses.definitionCN: 对身体部位持续施压，例如止血
senses.example: Direct compression stopped the bleeding.
senses.exampleCN: 直接压迫止住了出血。
senses.why: The same physical act is used on tissue, and the noun keeps its literal force in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 同一个物理动作被用在组织上，这个名词在医学中保留了字面含义。

senses.title: Encoding sound and video
senses.definition: the process of reducing the bit rate of audio or video while keeping it usable
senses.definitionCN: 在保持可用性的前提下降低音频或视频码率的过程
senses.example: The stream uses compression to fit the bandwidth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流媒体用压缩来适应带宽。
senses.why: Media data behaves like any other data, and the engineering word carried over unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 媒体数据与其它数据一样，工程词原样搬了过来。

senses.title: Shortening a text
senses.definition: the reduction of a text or account to its essential points
senses.definitionCN: 把文本或叙述减到要点
senses.example: The summary is a compression of a long report.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要是对一份长报告的浓缩。
senses.why: Ideas are imagined as taking up space, so shortening them is called squeezing them.
senses.whyCN: 观念被想象成占空间的东西，因此缩短它们被叫作挤压。

senses.title: The pressed state
senses.definition: the condition of being pressed tightly together, as of a spring or a seal
senses.definitionCN: 被紧密压在一起的状态，如弹簧或密封件
senses.example: The seal works by compression against the flange.
senses.exampleCN: 这个密封件靠压紧在法兰上起作用。
senses.why: The result of pressing is a state, and machine design needs a noun for that state.
senses.whyCN: 压的结果是一种状态，机械设计需要名词来表示这种状态。

intro.en: Compression comes from French or Latin compressio, from compressus, the past participle of comprimere, to press together, built from com, together, and premere, to press.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语或拉丁语 compressio，源自 comprimere「压到一起」的过去分词 compressus；该动词由 com「一起」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together or with, and here it marks the two sides of a material being brought into contact.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「一起、共同」，在这里标出材料两侧被压到接触。

items.en: Premere meant to press, squeeze or push down, and it is the same stem behind English press and pressure.
items.cn: 这个词意为压、挤、按下，也是英语 press 与 pressure 背后的同一词干。

items.en: The compound verb meant to press together or compress, used of physical objects and of shortened speech.
items.cn: 这一复合动词意为压到一起、压缩，既用于实物，也用于缩短的言语。

items.en: The noun named the act of pressing together, and French carried it into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词指压到一起的动作，十六世纪由法语带入英语。

items.en: Mechanics made compression the opposite of tension, naming the force that shortens a member; the exact date is uncertain and is tied to the formation of stress analysis.
items.cn: 力学使 compression 成为 tension 的反面，用来指缩短构件的力；确切年代不确定，只知随应力分析一并定型。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to data and media, where files are made smaller by encoding.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这个词用于数据与媒体，文件通过编码变小。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like compression; the second group names neighbouring ideas of pressing and shrinking.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「compression」相近；第二组是与「压紧、缩小」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb for pressing something smaller or shortening data.
entries.definitionCN: 指把东西压小或缩短数据的动词。

entries.definition: A machine that squeezes gas into a smaller volume.
entries.definitionCN: 指把气体压进更小体积的机器。

entries.definition: Relating to force that presses material together.
entries.definitionCN: 指与把材料压拢的力有关的。

entries.definition: Sympathy for suffering; it shares the prefix but comes from a word for feeling, not pressing.
entries.definitionCN: 指对苦难的同情；共享前缀，但来自表示「感受」的词，而非压。

entries.definition: Force applied over an area, including the pressing force in a fluid or solid.
entries.definitionCN: 指施加在面积上的力，包括流体或固体中的压力。

entries.definition: To press from two sides so that something becomes narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 指从两侧压，使某物变窄。

entries.definition: The shortening of a text or the change of vapour into liquid; it shares the idea of making denser.
entries.definitionCN: 指文本的缩短或蒸汽变液体；共享「使更密」的意思。

entries.definition: The conversion of data into a more compact or usable form.
entries.definitionCN: 指把数据转换成更紧凑或可用的形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real press-together source, the real mechanics family and real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「压到一起」来源、真实力学同族词与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Com means together and premere means press, so compression is a pressing together.
normal.cn: 前缀意为一起，词根意为压，所以 compression 就是压到一起。

normal.en: Press, pressure and compression are three words from one pressing stem.
normal.cn: press、pressure 与 compression 是同一个「压」词干的三张面孔。

normal.en: Compression ratio belongs to engines, compression test to materials.
normal.cn: 压缩比属于发动机，压缩试验属于材料。

normal.en: Compression is the opposite of tension, one shortens and one lengthens.
normal.cn: 压缩与拉伸相对，一个使变短，一个使变长。

normal.en: Data compression squeezes a file the way a press squeezes foam.
normal.cn: 数据压缩压小文件，就像压机压小泡沫。

abstract.en: Compression is space removed from something without destroying it.
abstract.cn: 压缩是从某物里拿走空间，却不毁掉它。

abstract.en: Every column carries its load by being compressed every second.
abstract.cn: 每根柱子都靠每秒被压缩来承担荷载。

abstract.en: A good summary is compression that keeps the shape.
abstract.cn: 好的摘要是保住了形状的压缩。

examples.en: The test measures compression at three loads.
examples.cn: 这项试验在三种载荷下测量压缩。

examples.en: Lossless compression keeps every bit of the file.
examples.cn: 无损压缩保留文件的每一个比特。

examples.en: Too much compression cracked the foam core.
examples.cn: 压缩过度使泡沫芯开裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康普瑞申」——把东西「康」在一起、普瑞地压紧：压缩

root: 法语或拉丁语 compressio ← compressus（comprimere「压到一起」的过去分词）← com-「一起」+ premere「压」；premere 同族有 press「压」与 pressure「压力」。力学使它与 tension 相对，二十世纪又用于数据与媒体压缩；各义定型年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all reduce space or press things together: a physical squeeze, internal force, a file, a cylinder charge, a wound, a media stream, a long text and a seated seal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在减少空间或把东西压拢：物理挤压、内部压力、文件、气缸混合气、伤口、媒体流、长文本与压紧的密封件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two plates close on foam until it is half as thick.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块压板合拢压住泡沫，直到它只剩一半厚度。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SQUEEZE: the act of pressing and the pressed state that remains.
branches.cn: 物理挤压：压的动作，以及压完之后留下的压紧状态。

branches.en: THE INTERNAL FORCE: the push inside a column that holds the roof up.
branches.cn: 内部压力：柱子内部撑住屋顶的那股推力。

branches.en: THE SHRUNK SIGNAL: a file or a media stream made smaller by encoding.
branches.cn: 被压小的信号：通过编码变小的文件或媒体流。

branches.en: THE ENGINE CHARGE: gas squeezed in a cylinder before it burns.
branches.cn: 发动机充量：燃烧前在气缸里被压紧的气体。

branches.en: THE PRESSED BODY AND TEXT: a bandage on a wound, and a report cut to its points.
branches.cn: 被压的身体与文本：伤口上的绷带，以及删到要点的报告。

intro.en: Compression is a Latin noun of pressing, carried by French, and its stem still builds compressors and compressibility.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「压」的拉丁名词，经法语传入，其词干至今仍构成压缩机与可压缩性等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and premere are the real parts, comprimere the compound, and compressio the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 com- 与 premere 是真实构件，comprimere 是复合动词，compressio 是名词。

items.structure: Latin prefix, assimilated form of con-
items.example: The prefix brings the two sides together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把两侧带到一起。

items.example: The verb is the pressing core.
The compound is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是直接来源。

items.example: The noun entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成英语名词。

由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「压缩机」
由该名词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「抗压的」

definition_zh: 有害的；凶恶的；不祥的
definition_en: threatening harm or evil; sinister in effect or appearance
core_image: 巫婆炉火边抬起的阴冷目光
scene: 炉火忽暗，墙上的影子拉长了脖颈。 He gave the intruder a baleful stare.
sceneCN: 这里 baleful 指「凶恶的、不祥的」（第 1 个义项：带有威胁与恶意）；句意：他向闯入者投去阴狠的一瞥。

pos.zh: 有害的；凶恶的；不祥的

derivatives.zh: 不祥地；凶恶地（baleful + -ly）
凶恶；危害（baleful + -ness）
（废义）灾祸；悲恸（baleful 的词根名词）

senses.title: Sinister in expression
senses.definition: of a look or manner, menacing and full of malice
senses.definitionCN: 形容目光或神态充满威胁与恶意
senses.example: The cat fixed a baleful eye on the puppy.
senses.exampleCN: 猫恶狠狠地盯着那只小狗。
senses.why: The old noun bale meant sorrow and harm; the face that promises them is baleful.
senses.whyCN: 古名词 bale 意为灾殃与伤害，预示二者之脸即 baleful。

senses.title: Harmful in influence
senses.definition: of forces, policies, or powers, working injury or ruin
senses.definitionCN: 指势力、政策或权力造成伤害与毁灭
senses.example: Corruption proved a baleful influence on the port.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败对港口造成了恶劣影响。
senses.why: Old poetry paired bale with fire and ruin; the adjective kept the scope.
senses.whyCN: 古诗以 bale 配火与毁灭，形容词保留了这一广度。

senses.title: Deadly or destructive in effect
senses.definition: bringing death or destruction, in elevated or poetic use
senses.definitionCN: 书面或诗歌用法，指带来死亡或毁灭
senses.example: The plague's baleful progress emptied the city.
senses.exampleCN: 瘟疫肆虐，城市为之一空。
senses.why: The Germanic root meant destruction before it meant sadness.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼词根先表毁灭，后才转为悲恸。

senses.title: Ominous, boding ill
senses.definition: of signs or events, foretelling disaster
senses.definitionCN: 指征兆或事件预示灾祸
senses.example: A baleful moon rose over the burned ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 焦黑的山脊上升起一轮不祥的月。
senses.why: What threatens harm also announces it.
senses.whyCN: 威胁伤害之物，亦即宣告伤害之物。

senses.title: Sorrowful in the old poetry
senses.definition: in archaic use, full of misery or grief
senses.definitionCN: 古义中指充满悲惨与哀恸
senses.example: The widow's baleful cries filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 寡妇的悲号响彻大厅。
senses.why: Bale and woe were twins in medieval verse.
senses.whyCN: 中古诗歌里 bale 与 woe 是一对孪生词。

senses.title: Of speech, poisoning with malice
senses.definition: of words or counsel, crafted to injure the hearer
senses.definitionCN: 指言语或进言蓄意加害听者
senses.example: A baleful whisper turned the brothers against each other.
senses.exampleCN: 一句恶毒的耳语让兄弟反目。
senses.why: Evil that travels by ear is still evil.
senses.whyCN: 借耳朵行凶的恶，仍是恶。

senses.title: Of institutions, corrosive over time
senses.definition: of systems or customs, slowly corrupting those inside them
senses.definitionCN: 指制度或习俗日积月累地腐蚀其中之人
senses.example: Critics called the quota a baleful inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称那套配额是贻害已久的遗产。
senses.why: Slow harm borrows the language of active evil.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢之害借用了主动之恶的语言。

senses.title: In fantasy and fiction, dark magic
senses.definition: a stock adjective for dark spells and cursed objects
senses.definitionCN: 奇幻文学中形容黑暗法术与诅咒之物的惯用词
senses.example: The ring's baleful glow warned the hobbit away.
senses.exampleCN: 魔戒凶光闪闪，警告霍比特人退后。
senses.why: Genre writing inherited the Gothic dictionary wholesale.
senses.whyCN: 类型写作整体继承了哥特的词库。

intro.en: Baleful is the archaic noun bale, evil or sorrow, from Old English bealu, plus -ful; bealu goes back to a Germanic root for destruction, cognate with Old Norse bölvun, curse.
intro.cn: baleful 由古名词 bale（邪恶、悲恸）加 -ful 构成；bale 出自古英语 bealu，可追溯至日耳曼语表「毁灭」的词根，与古诺斯语 bölvun「诅咒」同源。

items.en: The harm-root is reconstructed as balu-, destruction or wickedness.
items.cn: 「伤害」词根被重构为 balu-「毁灭、邪恶」。

items.en: bealu was a strong poetic word for evil, torment, and destruction, common in Beowulf.
items.cn: bealu 是表邪恶、苦难、毁灭的强诗歌词，常见于《贝奥武甫》。

items.en: Old Norse bölvun, curse, and boli, mischief, keep the root alive next door.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 bölvun「诅咒」与 boli「祸害」在邻近语言中保存着词根。

items.en: Middle English bale named sorrow and hell-fire in romance and sermon alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 bale 在传奇与布道中兼指悲恸与地狱之火。

items.en: The adjective baleful formed early, attested before 1400.
items.cn: 形容词 baleful 早已形成，1400 年前已见于记载。

items.en: The noun bale of sorrow died out; baleful carries it alone, favoring stares and influences.
items.cn: 表悲恸的名词 bale 已消亡，唯 baleful 独承其义，多形容目光与影响。

note.en: Group one gathers the sorrow-bale family and the homograph trap; group two gathers the sinister scale.
note.cn: 第一组收「灾殃 bale」词族与同形词陷阱；第二组收阴恶刻度上的词。

entries.definition: the common noun for a bound bundle, unrelated in origin to the bale inside baleful.
entries.definitionCN: 常用名词「货包」，与 baleful 中的 bale 词源无关。

entries.definition: the dance; similar letters, Italian origin, no harm in it.
entries.definitionCN: 芭蕾；字母相近、源出意大利语，毫无凶恶之意。

entries.definition: in a baleful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 不祥地；凶恶地。

entries.definition: threatening evil, from the Latin left hand.
entries.definitionCN: 阴险不祥的，源自拉丁语「左」。

entries.definition: wishing harm to others.
entries.definitionCN: 心存恶意的。

entries.definition: ruinous; a near-twin from a different Old English root (bana, slayer).
entries.definitionCN: 致命的；近义孪生词，出自另一古英语词根 bana「杀戮者」。

entries.definition: evil in influence or disposition.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；恶毒的。

entries.definition: kindly and gracious; the antonym pole.
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈宽厚的；反义一极。

normalIntro.en: Read it as bale plus full: full of bale, the old word for harm.
normalIntro.cn: 读作 bale + full：盛满古义「灾殃」之物。

normal.en: bale here means sorrow and harm, not the hay bale.
normal.cn: 此处 bale 指灾殃悲恸，不是干草捆。

normal.en: a baleful stare is the classic collocation.
normal.cn: a baleful stare 是经典搭配。

normal.en: Compare baneful: same meaning, different Old English root.
normal.cn: 对照 baneful：同义而古英语词根不同。

normal.en: Beowulf keeps the root alive in bealu.
normal.cn: 《贝奥武甫》中的 bealu 保存着这个词根。

normal.en: Adverb and noun: balefully, balefulness.
normal.cn: 副词与名词：balefully、balefulness。

abstract.en: Feel the temperature drop when the eyes turn.
abstract.cn: 感觉目光转来时气温骤降。

abstract.en: Baleful is the shadow that arrives before its owner.
abstract.cn: baleful 是先于主人抵达的影子。

abstract.en: Hear the vowel lengthen, as menace does.
abstract.cn: 听那个长元音，一如威胁的绵长。

examples.en: A baleful fog swallowed the lighthouse beam.
examples.cn: 不祥的浓雾吞没了灯塔的光束。

examples.en: The usurper's baleful reign ended in a single night.
examples.cn: 篡位者的暴政在一夜之间覆灭。

examples.en: She spoke of the mine's baleful legacy of dust and debt.
examples.cn: 她谈起那座矿留下的粉尘与债务之祸。

root: baleful = bale（古义「灾殃、悲恸」，古英语 bealu）+ -ful。bealu 可追溯至原始日耳曼语词根 balu-「毁灭、邪恶」，与古诺斯语 bölvun「诅咒」同源；《贝奥武甫》等古英语诗歌常用。形容词于 1400 年前形成；后来名词 bale 消亡，唯 baleful 独存，与「货包」义的 bale 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread the old harm across registers: the evil eye, the corrupting influence, the deadly plague, the ominous moon, the archaic grief, poisoned words, corroding institutions, and fantasy's dark magic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项把古老的「害」铺展到各个语域：恶眼、腐蚀性影响、致命瘟疫、不祥之月、古义之悲、恶毒言语、侵蚀性制度，以及奇幻的黑暗魔法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: harm announced by a look before any blow falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：拳未落，眼先害人。

branches.en: THE FACE AND VOICE SIDE: stares and whispers that wound.
branches.cn: 面容言语一面：伤人的目光与耳语。

branches.en: THE FORCE SIDE: influences, plagues, and institutions that ruin.
branches.cn: 势力一面：致毁的影响、瘟疫与制度。

branches.en: THE OMEN SIDE: signs that promise disaster.
branches.cn: 征兆一面：预告灾祸的迹象。

branches.en: THE GRIEF SIDE: the archaic sorrowful use.
branches.cn: 悲恸一面：古义的哀伤用法。

branches.en: THE FICTION SIDE: genre magic wearing the old word.
branches.cn: 虚构一面：披着古词的类型魔法。

intro.en: Baleful is a native English compound: old noun bale plus suffix -ful.
intro.cn: baleful 是本族英语复合词：古名词 bale 加后缀 -ful。

latinIntro.en: No Latin is involved; the adjective was built before Chaucer, from purely Germanic parts.
latinIntro.cn: 与拉丁语无关；该形容词在乔叟之前已由纯日耳曼成分构成。

senses.title: The large hairy bee

senses.title: A clumsy person

intro.en: Bumblebee joins an old humming word with the plain name of the insect.

items.en: Bumbeln means to hum or blunder about.

items.en: Writers separate it from the honeybee.

items.en: Local names include humblebee.

definition_zh: 停火；停火命令或协议；停火状态；引申指激烈攻击的暂停
definition_en: an order or agreement to stop shooting, the state of not shooting, or a temporary halt of intense attacks
core_image: 阵地上密集的曳光弹突然消失，枪管仍在冒烟，士兵从掩体后探出头
scene: 清晨的街区里，广播喇叭传出一段命令，交火双方的枪声先后停下，居民从地下室慢慢走出来。 The mediator announced a ceasefire, an order to stop shooting, and the guns fell silent by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 ceasefire 指「双方停止射击的命令或安排」（第 1 个义项：使火力停止的约定）；句意为调解人宣布停火，到中午枪声就停了。可辨识物件：广播喇叭、掩体、步枪、地下室出口、停下的弹壳。

pos.zh: 停火；停火命令或协议；停火状态（可数，复数 ceasefires）

停止；中止

senses.title: An order or agreement to stop shooting
senses.titleCN: 停止射击的命令或约定
senses.definition: an instruction or arrangement by which opposing forces stop firing, usually for a set time or area
senses.definitionCN: 交战双方停止射击的指令或安排，通常限定时间或区域
senses.example: The mediator announced a ceasefire, and the shooting stopped by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 调解人宣布停火，到中午枪声就停了。
senses.why: cease is 'to stop' and fire is 'shooting', so the compound names the stopping of shooting directly.
senses.whyCN: cease 是「停止」，fire 是「射击」，因此这个复合词直接命名「停止射击」。

senses.title: The state of no firing
senses.definition: the condition in which no shots are being fired along a line or in an area
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条战线或某个区域内没有射击的状态
senses.example: A fragile ceasefire held while the negotiators met.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判代表会面期间，一个脆弱的停火得以维持。
senses.why: a command creates a state, and English often lets the same noun name both the order and the condition it produces.
senses.whyCN: 命令造成状态，英语常让同一个名词既指命令，也指它造成的状态。

senses.title: A written or spoken agreement
senses.titleCN: 书面或口头的停火协议
senses.definition: a formal or informal deal that fixes when and where firing will stop
senses.definitionCN: 确定何时何地停止射击的正式或非正式约定
senses.example: The ceasefire agreement set a corridor for aid.
senses.exampleCN: 停火协议划出了一条援助走廊。
senses.why: the word is used for the document as well as the act, as with treaty and armistice.
senses.whyCN: 和 treaty、armistice 一样，这个词既指行为，也指文书。

senses.title: A unilateral declaration
senses.definition: a halt declared by one side without the other's consent, often to gain political advantage
senses.definitionCN: 一方未经对方同意而宣布的停止射击，常为取得政治优势
senses.example: The government offered a unilateral ceasefire at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在午夜单方面提出停火。
senses.why: one party can stop shooting alone; the word does not require reciprocity, though it often implies it.
senses.whyCN: 一方可以独自停止射击；这个词并不要求对等，尽管通常暗示对等。

senses.title: A humanitarian pause
senses.definition: a short, local halt arranged so that aid, evacuation or burial can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 为援助、撤离或掩埋而安排的短时局部停火
senses.example: A humanitarian ceasefire let convoys cross the front.
senses.exampleCN: 人道主义停火让车队穿过前线。
senses.why: when the purpose is saving lives rather than settling the war, the compound takes a humanitarian modifier.
senses.whyCN: 当目的在救命而非解决战争时，这个复合词会带人道主义修饰语。

senses.title: A ceasefire that is broken
senses.definition: a halt that fails, with firing resuming and blame traded by both sides
senses.definitionCN: 未能维持、射击恢复且双方互相指责的停火
senses.example: The ceasefire collapsed after a single mortar round.
senses.exampleCN: 一发迫击炮弹就让停火崩溃。
senses.why: a pause is fragile because it rests on restraint, not on settlement; the word therefore appears with collapse and violation.
senses.whyCN: 暂停是脆弱的，因为它依赖克制而非解决；因此这个词常与「崩溃」「违反」搭配。

senses.title: Figurative halt of intense attacks
senses.definition: by extension, a pause in a fierce non-military campaign such as cyber attacks or hostile publicity
senses.definitionCN: 引申指网络攻击或敌意宣传等非军事激烈行动的暂停
senses.example: The platforms called a ceasefire in the disinformation war.
senses.exampleCN: 各平台在虚假信息战中呼吁停火。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the gunfire image and applies it to any exchange of blows at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留枪火意象，把它用于任何远程交火。

senses.title: Abstraction: a cooling of a conflict system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：冲突系统的冷却
senses.definition: any agreed reduction of intensity in a hostile system, seen as a cooling rather than a cure
senses.definitionCN: 敌对系统中任何约定的强度下降，被视为降温而非治愈
senses.example: A ceasefire lowers the temperature, but the dispute remains.
senses.exampleCN: 停火降低了温度，但争端仍在。
senses.why: the deepest sense is thermodynamic rather than legal: intensity falls, structure stays.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是热力学式的而非法律式的：强度下降，结构不变。

intro.en: Ceasefire joins an Old French verb of stopping to the native English word for fire. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceasefire 把古法语「停止」动词与英语本族词「火」连接起来，属近代复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old French cesser 'to stop, give way' came from Latin cessare, a frequentative of cedere 'to go, yield'.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser「停止、让出」来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「行走、让出」的反复动词。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, withdraw, yield'; cessare repeated the action, giving the sense of holding off or stopping.
items.cn: cedere 意为「行走、退去、让出」；cessare 表示反复，产生「退开、停止」之义。

items.en: Fire descends from Old English fȳr and Proto-Germanic *fōr; the Indo-European ancestor is usually reconstructed as *perjos, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: fire 承自英语 fȳr 与原始日耳曼语 *fōr；其印欧祖形通常重构为 *perjos，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The compound cease-fire appeared in military writing in the early twentieth century, when industrialized armies needed a word for a scheduled halt of artillery.
items.cn: cease-fire 这一复合词在二十世纪初的军事写作中出现，当时工业化军队需要一个词来指按计划停止炮击。

items.en: After the First World War the term moved into diplomacy and then into figurative use for any intense campaign.
items.cn: 第一次世界大战之后，这个词进入外交领域，随后引申用于任何激烈行动。

items.en: Source uncertain (coinage date): dictionaries differ on the first printed use, and the Indo-European roots of both fire and cedere are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词年代）：辞书对最早印刷用例说法不一，且 fire 与 cedere 的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds stop-fighting terms that overlap with ceasefire; group two holds the wider diplomatic and military ideas around it.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ceasefire 重叠的停止战斗类词；第二组是围绕它的更广的外交与军事概念。

entries.definition: Simply to stop or bring to an end; it needs an object, as in cease firing, and carries no agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指停止或终止；需要宾语，如停止射击，且不含约定之意。

entries.definition: The act of stopping, often used in phrases such as cessation of hostilities; it is more formal and less specific than ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指停止的行为，常用于「停止敌对行动」等短语；比 ceasefire 更正式、更宽泛。

entries.definition: Agreements limiting weapons types or numbers; they shape the future of a conflict rather than stop present firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制武器种类或数量的协定；它塑造冲突的未来，而非停止当下的射击。

entries.definition: A short agreed stop in fighting; it is older and plainer, and often briefer than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指约定短时停止战斗；更古老、更口语，通常比停火更短暂。

entries.definition: A formal suspension of hostilities, usually while peace is negotiated; it is generally more binding than a ceasefire.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式休战，通常在谈判和平期间；一般比停火更具约束力。

entries.definition: A settlement that ends a war and fixes the postwar order; a ceasefire only stops the shooting.
entries.definitionCN: 指结束战争、确定战后秩序的解决方案；停火只停止射击。

entries.definition: A deliberate lowering of tension or force; it may occur without any formal halt in firing.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意降低紧张或武力强度；不一定伴随正式停火。

entries.definition: An area where fighting is excluded by agreement; it is a spatial arrangement that a ceasefire may protect.
entries.definitionCN: 指经约定排除战斗的区域；这是空间安排，停火可用于保护它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real words, the Latin chain behind cease and the compound's modern military setting.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词、cease 背后的拉丁链条，以及这个复合词的近代军事背景。

normal.en: cease 'stop' + fire 'shooting': the name says exactly what stops.
normal.cn: cease「停止」+ fire「射击」：这个名字直接说出停的是什么。

normal.en: Cease goes back through French to Latin cessare, a repeated cedere, 'to withdraw'.
normal.cn: cease 经法语上溯拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去」的反复形式。

normal.en: The family runs cease, cessation, ceasefire, fire, gunfire, firepower.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cease、cessation、ceasefire、fire、gunfire、firepower。

normal.en: A ceasefire is a pause, not a settlement: the war is still legally alive.
normal.cn: 停火是暂停而非解决：战争在法律上仍然存在。

normal.en: Typical partners are declare, broker, violate and collapse.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「宣布」「斡旋」「违反」「崩溃」。

abstract.en: Picture a loud machine switched to silent mode without being unplugged.
abstract.cn: 想象一台吵闹的机器被调到静音，却并未拔掉电源。

abstract.en: Picture a fever brought down by medicine: the disease is still in the body.
abstract.cn: 想象用药物把高烧退下：病还在体内。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted in a game: play stops, but the score is unchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象比赛中举起一只手：比赛停了，比分未变。

examples.en: Both sides accused each other of breaking the ceasefire.
examples.cn: 双方都指责对方破坏停火。

examples.en: The ceasefire allowed aid trucks to reach the valley.
examples.cn: 停火让援助卡车得以抵达山谷。

examples.en: A ceasefire without monitoring rarely lasts.
examples.cn: 没有监督的停火很少能持久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cease（停止）+ fire（开火）」——停止开火 → 停火

root: cease 经古法语 cesser 来自拉丁 cessare，是 cedere「退去、让出」的反复动词；fire 来自古英语 fȳr，属日耳曼语本族词。复合为「停止射击」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the literal order to stop shooting, through the state and the document, to unilateral and humanitarian versions, to a broken halt, a metaphor for any campaign and finally a general cooling of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的停止射击命令出发，经过停火状态与文书，再到单方面与人道主义变体，再到被破坏的停火，再到任何行动的比喻，最后落到冲突的普遍降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of rifles lowered at once while smoke still rises from the barrels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排步枪同时放下，枪管仍在冒烟。

branches.en: ORDER AND CONDITION: the command creates the quiet it names.
branches.cn: 命令与状态：命令造出它所命名的安静。

branches.en: PAPER OR ONE VOICE: a deal can be signed by two or offered by one.
branches.cn: 纸面或单方：协议可由两方签署，也可由一方提出。

branches.en: MERCY AND FAILURE: a pause to save lives can still break under one shell.
branches.cn: 仁慈与失败：为救命的暂停仍可能被一发炮弹打破。

branches.en: BORROWED GUNFIRE: any distant exchange of blows can be paused this way.
branches.cn: 借来的枪火：任何远程交火都能这样暂停。

branches.en: COOLING, NOT CURE: intensity falls while the structure of the dispute remains.
branches.cn: 降温而非治愈：强度下降，争端结构仍在。

intro.en: Ceasefire is a transparent English compound of a Latin-derived verb and a native noun, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: ceasefire 是透明的英语复合词，由拉丁来源动词与本族名词构成，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare and cedere build cease, cessation, cession and concede; fire has no Latin root and is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cessare 与 cedere 构成 cease、cessation、cession 与 concede；fire 无拉丁词根，属日耳曼语。

items.structure: cease (Old French cesser, from Latin cessare)
items.meaning: to stop, bring to an end
items.example: The battery ceased firing at dusk.
The Latin verb implied repeated yielding.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词含反复退让之意。

items.example: The root also underlies concede and cession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也构成 concede 与 cession。

items.example: The fire from the ridge pinned the patrol.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的火力压制了巡逻队。

items.meaning: the volume of fire a force can deliver
items.meaningCN: 一支部队能投送的火力
items.exampleCN: 他们的火力迫使对方撤退。

items.example: The ceasefire agreement named two monitors.
items.exampleCN: 停火协议指定了两名监督员。

items.meaning: the same term in older style

definition_zh: 叶子（总称）；叶丛；装饰用枝叶
definition_en: the leaves of a plant or of many plants taken as a mass; cut branches used for decoration
core_image: 一棵树的所有叶片连成一片会摇动的绿色表面，风过时整片一起翻动
scene: 入秋以后叶片由绿转铜再转金，远看整片林子像被重新上了色。 Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
sceneCN: 这里 foliage 指「一棵或一片植物上全部叶子的总称」（第 1 个义项：把叶子作为整体看待的叶丛）；句意为秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。

pos.zh: 叶子（总称）；叶丛
（花艺、装饰用）切叶
