senses.title: All the leaves of a plant
senses.titleCN: 一株或一片植物的叶子的总称
senses.definition: the leaves of a plant or group of plants considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一株或一群植物的叶子作为整体看待
senses.example: Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。
senses.why: Foliage is a collective noun: it never counts leaves one by one, it sees them as one surface.
senses.whyCN: foliage 是集合名词：它从不一片一片地数叶子，而是把叶子看成一张表面。

senses.title: The leafy canopy as a layer
senses.titleCN: 树冠里由叶子组成的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of leaves that fills a crown and shades what is below
senses.definitionCN: 树冠中填满枝叶、遮住下方的那一层
senses.example: Sparrows hid in the dense foliage of the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 麻雀藏在树篱茂密的叶丛里。
senses.why: Once the mass is seen from below or above, it becomes a layer with depth and shade, not just a list of parts.
senses.whyCN: 从下方或上方看这团叶子时，它就成了有厚度、有阴影的一层，而不只是一堆部件。

senses.title: Leaves valued for their colour
senses.titleCN: 因颜色而被观赏的叶子
senses.definition: leaves regarded as colour, especially in autumn or in ornamental planting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作色彩来欣赏的叶子，尤指秋叶或观赏栽植
senses.example: Tourists come for the autumn foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 游客为秋叶而来。
senses.why: When colour is the point, the word moves from botany to scenery, and the leaf becomes a patch of paint.
senses.whyCN: 当重点是颜色，这个词就从植物学移向风景，叶子也成了一块颜料。

senses.title: Cut branches for decoration
senses.definition: stems and leaves cut for floristry or display
senses.definitionCN: 为花艺或陈列剪下的枝与叶
senses.example: The florist ordered cut foliage for the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 花艺师为大堂订了切叶。
senses.why: A trade term treats the mass as material: it is harvested, graded and sold like any other stock.
senses.whyCN: 行业术语把这团叶当材料：像别的货品一样采收、分级、出售。

senses.title: Leafy material eaten by animals
senses.definition: branches and leaves used as fodder
senses.definitionCN: 用作饲料的枝叶
senses.example: Goats browse the lower foliage of the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 山羊啃食树下部枝叶。
senses.why: Husbandry turns the same mass into feed, measured by what a animal can reach.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧把它变成饲料，按动物能够到的高度来衡量。

senses.title: Leaf ornament in art
senses.definition: leaf forms used as ornament in architecture or design
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与设计中被用作装饰的叶形
senses.example: The capital is carved with acanthus foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头刻着茛苕叶饰。
senses.why: Ornament keeps only the outline of leaves, so the word comes to mean a pattern rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 装饰只保留叶子的轮廓，词义于是变成图案而非植物。

senses.title: A plant grown for its leaves
senses.titleCN: 以观叶为目的栽种的植物
senses.definition: a plant cultivated mainly for its leaves rather than flowers
senses.definitionCN: 主要因叶而非花而栽种的植物
senses.example: Foliage plants fill the shaded border.
senses.exampleCN: 观叶植物填满了背阴花坛。
senses.why: Horticulture splits plants by the organ that sells, and the leaf group takes the mass noun as a label.
senses.whyCN: 园艺按出售的器官给植物分类，观叶这一类就用这个集合名词作标签。

senses.title: Cover and concealment
senses.titleCN: 被枝叶遮住而形成的掩蔽
senses.definition: the concealment that a mass of leaves provides
senses.definitionCN: 成片叶子提供的遮蔽
senses.example: The nest was lost in foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 巢藏在叶丛深处看不见。
senses.why: A mass thick enough to hide a nest becomes a place, so the word shifts from material to cover.
senses.whyCN: 厚到能藏住鸟巢的一团叶就成了一个地方，词义从材料转为掩蔽。

intro.en: Foliage comes from Old French feuillage, from feuille 'leaf', from Latin folium 'leaf'. The Latin noun is linked to Greek phyllon, but the deeper origin is unsettled.
intro.cn: foliage 来自古法语 feuillage，源于 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」。这个拉丁名词与希腊 phyllon 有联系，但更深来源未定。

items.en: Folium meant 'leaf'. Its relation to Greek phyllon 'leaf' is generally believed, yet no single older root has been demonstrated.
items.cn: folium 意为「叶」。它与希腊 phyllon「叶」的联系一般认为成立，但更古老的单一词根尚未得到证明。

items.en: The plural folia 'leaves' was felt as a collective, which prepared the way for a mass noun.
items.cn: 复数 folia「叶子」有集合意味，为后来的集合名词铺了路。

items.en: Old French feuille 'leaf' kept the Latin sense; its collective derivative feuillage named the mass of leaves.
items.cn: 古法语 feuille「叶」保留了拉丁义；它的集合派生词 feuillage 指成片的叶。

items.en: English borrowed foliage in the sixteenth century for leaves in general, and later for cut branches in floristry.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 foliage，泛指叶子，后来又指花艺中的切叶。

items.en: Architectural handbooks extended it to carved leaf patterns, where only the outline survives.
items.cn: 建筑手册把它扩展到雕刻的叶形图案，那里只剩轮廓。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link between folium and phyllon is a general belief rather than a proven derivation, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：folium 与 phyllon 的联系只是一般看法，并非已证实的派生；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates relatives built on Latin folium from one false friend; group two holds words for leaves and leaf masses.
note.cn: 第一组区分由拉丁 folium 构成的同族词与一个假朋友；第二组指叶子与叶丛的说法。

entries.definition: From folium: a leaf of paper or a book format; the plant sense was lost when it named pages.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 folium：指一张纸或书的开本；转指纸页后植物义消失。

entries.definition: Portare 'to carry' plus folium: a case for loose sheets, now also a set of investments.
entries.definitionCN: portare「携带」加 folium：装散页的夹子，今也指一组投资。

entries.definition: Relating to leaves, as foliar feeding; it describes leaves rather than naming a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 与叶有关的，如叶面施肥；它描述叶，不命名叶丛。

entries.definition: From Latin filum 'thread', which gave the idea of a line of documents; nothing to do with leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 filum「线」，引申为一列文件，与叶子无关。

entries.definition: The plain plural that counts individual leaves; foliage never counts.
entries.definitionCN: 普通复数，一片一片地数；foliage 从不计数。

entries.definition: An English formation on leaf plus -age, close in sense but far rarer than foliage.
entries.definitionCN: 由 leaf 加 -age 的英语构词，意义接近，但远比 foliage 少见。

entries.definition: The whole upper layer of a tree or forest, branches included; foliage is the leaf part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指树或林的上层，含枝条；foliage 是其中的叶部。

entries.definition: Green plants as a pleasant sight; foliage is the leaf mass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 作为悦目景色的绿色植物；foliage 是叶丛本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and the real horticultural terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁词根与真实园艺术语。

normal.en: Latin folium 'leaf' + -age (collective): a mass of leaves.
normal.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」+ -age（集合）：成片的叶子。

normal.en: The family: foliar, foliate, defoliate, foliation.
normal.cn: 同族：foliar、foliate、defoliate、foliation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: dense foliage, autumn foliage, foliage plant, cut foliage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：茂密叶丛、秋叶、观叶植物、切叶。

normal.en: The same root gives folio and portfolio, both about sheets of paper.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 folio 与 portfolio，都与纸页有关。

normal.en: Florists sell cut foliage as material, the same way nurseries sell foliage plants.
normal.cn: 花艺师把切叶当材料卖，苗圃则卖观叶植物。

abstract.en: Picture one green surface spread over a whole wood, with no single leaf visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片森林上铺着一张绿表面，看不到单独一片叶。

abstract.en: Picture autumn as a painter repainting that surface from green to copper.
abstract.cn: 想象秋天是一位画家，把那层表面从绿改涂成铜色。

abstract.en: Picture a page and a leaf sharing one word because both are thin and flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸与一片叶共用一个词，因为两者都薄而平。

examples.en: The hedge keeps its foliage through the coldest months.
examples.cn: 这道树篱在最冷的几个月里仍保留叶丛。

examples.en: Cut foliage is sold by weight at the flower market.
examples.cn: 切叶在花市按重量出售。

examples.en: Acid rain damaged the foliage of the upland forest.
examples.cn: 酸雨损害了高地森林的叶丛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛利（foli）叶 + 集合（age）」——一大团叶子 → 叶丛；叶子总称

root: 古法语 feuillage 来自 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」；folium 与希腊 phyllon 的联系一般认为成立，更深词根未定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat leaves as one mass, then as shade, colour, cut material, fodder, ornament, a plant class and finally a hiding place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都先把叶子当成一团，再依次当作阴影、颜色、切材、饲料、纹样、植物类别，最后当作藏身之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous green surface made of countless leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：由无数叶片连成的一整张绿色表面。

branches.en: MASS INTO LAYER: a crowd of leaves becomes a canopy with depth.
branches.cn: 成团成层：一堆叶子变成有厚度的一层。

branches.en: COLOUR: the same mass is valued as paint on a landscape.
branches.cn: 颜色：同一团叶被当作风景上的颜料。

branches.en: MATERIAL: cut for the vase or browsed by animals, leaves become stock or feed.
branches.cn: 材料：剪进花瓶或被牲畜啃食，叶子成了货品或饲料。

branches.en: PATTERN AND CLASS: art keeps the outline, horticulture keeps the label.
branches.cn: 纹样与类别：艺术保留轮廓，园艺保留标签。

branches.en: COVER: thick enough to hide a nest, the mass becomes a place.
branches.cn: 掩蔽：厚到能藏巢，这团叶就成了一个地方。

intro.en: Foliage is Latin folium plus a French collective suffix; the root also builds the vocabulary of pages and of defoliation.
intro.cn: foliage 是拉丁 folium 加法语集合后缀；这个词根还构成纸页与落叶方面的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin folium 'leaf' gives folia, foliaris and foliatus; -age marks a collective mass in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」给出 folia、foliaris 与 foliatus；-age 在法语中表示集合。

items.example: The root names the flat green organ.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指扁平的绿色器官。

items.example: The plural was felt as a mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数带有集合意味。

items.example: It turns a single leaf into a mass.
A foliated capital shows carved leaves.
items.exampleCN: 有叶饰的柱头刻着叶子。

definition_zh: 气流；空气的流动；上升或下沉的气流；思潮（比喻义）
definition_en: a moving stream of air, especially one that can be felt or that carries heat, moisture or particles
core_image: 门缝下钻进来的一线冷空气，贴着地面滑行，把桌上的薄纸轻轻掀起
scene: 清晨的走廊里，一张薄纸被看不见的流动推着滑过桌面，学生说 A cold air current slid under the door and lifted the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 air current 指「一股正在流动的空气」（第 1 个义项：可以感觉到、并能带动轻物的空气流）；句意为一股冷气流从门缝下钻进来，把纸掀了起来。图中可辨识物件：门缝、薄纸、桌面、气流箭头。

pos.zh: 气流；空气流（可数，复数 air currents）

derivatives.zh: 流；水流；电流 / 当前的
目前；当前（由「当前」义而来）
空气流；气流流量
通风的；轻盈的
无空气的；闷不透风的

senses.title: A moving stream of air
senses.definition: a body of air that moves from one place to another and can be felt or can move light objects
senses.definitionCN: 从一处移向另一处的空气，可以被感觉到，也能推动轻物
senses.example: A thin air current made the curtain sway by the open window.
senses.exampleCN: 一股细微的气流让窗边的窗帘轻轻摆动。
senses.why: Current means 'running', so an air current is literally air that is running from place to place.
senses.whyCN: current 意为「奔跑的」，因此 air current 字面上就是「正在跑的空气」。

senses.title: A rising current
senses.definition: a column of warm air that rises because it is lighter than the air around it
senses.definitionCN: 因比周围空气轻而上升的一柱暖空气
senses.example: Gliders circle inside a rising air current to gain height.
senses.exampleCN: 滑翔机在上升气流里盘旋以获取高度。
senses.why: The same phrase covers any moving air; meteorology adds the direction, which is upward for a thermal.
senses.whyCN: 同一短语可指任何流动的空气；气象学加上方向，热气流的上升方向便是向上。

senses.title: A descending current
senses.definition: a flow of air that sinks toward the ground, often cool and dry
senses.definitionCN: 向地面下沉的空气流，通常干而凉
senses.example: The descending air current cleared the sky behind the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 下沉气流把风暴后方的天空清空了。
senses.why: Dense, cooled air falls, so meteorologists name the downward branch of a circulation an air current too.
senses.whyCN: 变冷变密的空气下沉，气象学家便把环流的下行分支同样称为气流。

senses.title: A local horizontal flow
senses.definition: a small-scale flow such as a sea breeze or a valley wind that runs roughly parallel to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 海风或谷风这类大致沿地面平行的局部流动
senses.example: A sea air current cools the town every summer afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 每天夏日午后，一股海风气流让小镇凉快下来。
senses.why: Local circulations complete their loop horizontally, so the general phrase is used with a direction word.
senses.whyCN: 局地环流在地面附近水平完成循环，因此这个泛称常与方向词连用。

senses.title: Indoor air movement
senses.definition: air set in motion inside a room by a fan, an open window or a temperature difference
senses.definitionCN: 由风扇、开窗或温差在房间内带动的空气
senses.example: A weak air current from the vent kept the room from feeling stale.
senses.exampleCN: 通风口送出的微弱气流让房间不至于闷。
senses.why: Buildings are small fluid systems, so the same two words describe ventilation on a room scale.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是小尺度的流体系统，因此同样的两个词也描述房间尺度的通风。

senses.title: A high-altitude current
senses.definition: a fast, narrow band of air in the upper atmosphere that steers weather systems
senses.definitionCN: 高层大气中快速而狭窄的空气带，它引导天气系统移动
senses.example: Aircraft save fuel by riding a strong high air current eastward.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机借助强劲的高空气流向东飞行以节省燃料。
senses.why: At altitude the same moving air becomes a jet, and the general compound still serves as the plain description.
senses.whyCN: 在高空，同样的流动空气变成急流，而这个泛称仍可作朴素描述。

senses.title: Turbulence in flight
senses.titleCN: 飞行中遇到的气流颠簸
senses.definition: an uneven flow of air that shakes an aircraft as it passes through
senses.definitionCN: 飞机穿过时使其颠簸的不均匀空气流
senses.example: The seatbelt sign came on as the plane hit a rough air current.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机遇到强烈气流时，系好安全带指示灯亮了。
senses.why: For passengers the current is felt as a jolt, so the physical phrase also names the experience.
senses.whyCN: 对乘客来说，气流表现为一阵颠簸，因此这个物理短语也指这种体验。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a widespread tendency of thinking or feeling that moves through a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人乃至社会中移动扩散的思想或情绪倾向
senses.example: An air current of reform ran through the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一股要求改革的思潮贯穿了整个会议。
senses.why: The metaphor treats public opinion as a fluid, so ideas can drift and carry others along.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把舆论当成流体，于是思想可以漂移，并带着其他想法一起走。

intro.en: Air current is an English compound of two borrowings: air, which came through Old French from Latin aer and Greek aēr, and current, from Latin currere 'to run'. The phrase itself is a modern descriptive compound rather than a single inherited word.
intro.cn: air current 是由两个借词构成的英语复合短语：air 经古法语来自拉丁 aer 与希腊 aēr，current 来自拉丁 currere「跑」。这个短语本身是现代描述性组合，不是单一传承词。

items.en: Aēr meant the lower, misty air, as opposed to aithēr, the bright upper sky; the deeper origin of aēr is not established.
items.cn: aēr 指低处朦胧的空气，与指明亮上天的 aithēr 相对；aēr 的更早来源未得到证明。

items.en: Latin aer 'air' was borrowed from Greek and passed through Old French into Middle English as air.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aer「空气」借自希腊语，再经古法语进入中古英语，成为 air。

items.en: Currere meant 'to run', with the present participle currens 'running'; the noun current first named a running course, then water, air and electricity.
items.cn: currere 意为「跑」，现在分词 currens 意为「奔跑的」；名词 current 先指奔流的路线，再指水、空气与电流。

items.en: Air and current were joined in English to describe moving air; the combination is transparent to any speaker and needs no separate etymology.
items.cn: air 与 current 在英语中组合起来描述流动的空气；这个组合对任何使用者都一目了然，无需另立词源。

items.en: The phrase became common in nineteenth-century weather writing, but the exact first use and the period when it fixed as a term are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个短语在 19 世纪天气文献中变得常见，但确切的最早使用及其固定为术语的年代均不确定。

note.en: Group one holds other air-plus-noun compounds that look almost identical; group two holds plain wind words that differ in force or origin.
note.cn: 第一组是其他「空气 + 名词」的复合词，看起来几乎一样；第二组是表示风、力度或来源有别的普通词。

entries.definition: A fast-moving stream of air, often written as one word; it stresses speed and continuity more than the general phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 快速移动的空气流，常写作一个词；比泛称更强调速度与连续性。

entries.definition: The movement or measured volume of air through a system such as a duct or an engine.
entries.definitionCN: 空气通过管道或发动机等系统的流动或其计量体积。

entries.definition: A concentrated, forceful stream of air blown from a nozzle.
entries.definitionCN: 从喷嘴吹出的集中而有力的空气流。

entries.definition: A region of descending or disturbed air that causes an aircraft to drop; it names the rough patch, not the flow itself.
entries.definitionCN: 使飞机下坠的下沉或扰动空气区；它指那块颠簸区，而不是流动本身。

entries.definition: Natural air moving outdoors, usually named by direction and strength; an air current can be indoor or local.
entries.definitionCN: 户外自然流动的空气，常以方向和强度命名；air current 可以是室内的或局地的。

entries.definition: A light, pleasant wind; it is a kind of air current with a low speed.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔宜人的风；是速度较低的一种气流。

entries.definition: A brief, sudden increase in wind speed; it is an event, not a steady current.
entries.definitionCN: 风速短暂而突然的增强；是一次事件，而非稳定的气流。

entries.definition: A current of cool air inside a building, often through a gap; the British spelling is draught.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部常从缝隙进入的冷空气流；英式拼写为 draught。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real borrowed roots, real compounds and real weather collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的借词词根、真实复合词与真实天气搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: air from Greek aēr through Latin aer; current from Latin currere 'to run'.
normal.cn: air 经拉丁 aer 上溯希腊 aēr；current 来自拉丁 currere「跑」。

normal.en: The phrase is transparent: air that is running, so direction and speed can always be added.
normal.cn: 这个短语一目了然：正在跑的空气，因此总能再加方向和速度。

normal.en: Weather writing adds the direction: rising, descending, upper-level air current.
normal.cn: 天气文献加上方向：上升、下沉、高空气流。

normal.en: The same current serves water and electricity, which is why the word feels familiar everywhere.
normal.cn: 同一个 current 也用于水流与电流，所以这个词处处似曾相识。

normal.en: A draft is the indoor cousin of an air current, usually colder and unwanted.
normal.cn: draft 是 air current 的室内亲戚，通常更冷、也更不受欢迎。

abstract.en: Picture a paper boat carried across a pond without any hand touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸船横过池塘，没有任何手去碰它。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour entering a room through a single open door and leaving by another.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言从一扇门进房，又从另一扇门离开。

abstract.en: Picture a glider climbing in a silent column of warm air above a dark field.
abstract.cn: 想象滑翔机在暗色田野上方一柱无声的暖空气里爬升。

examples.en: The balloon drifted east on a steady air current.
examples.cn: 气球借着一股稳定的气流向东飘去。

examples.en: A downward air current kept the valley drier than the ridge.
examples.cn: 下沉气流让山谷比山脊更干燥。

examples.en: The engineer measured the air current at the outlet of the duct.
examples.cn: 工程师测量了管道出口处的气流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「空气跑」——空气一跑起来，就是气流

root: 复合短语：air 经古法语来自拉丁 aer、再上溯希腊 aēr「低层空气」，aēr 的更早来源不确定；current 来自拉丁 currere「跑」的现在分词 currens。短语在 19 世纪天气文献中常见，确切最早使用与固定为术语的年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: air that runs becomes a current, and the same phrase covers rising, sinking, horizontal, indoor, high and turbulent flow, until it finally carries opinions instead of dust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：跑起来的空气成为气流，同一短语覆盖上升、下沉、水平、室内、高空与颠簸的流动，最后搬运的不再是灰尘而是观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin cold line of air slipping under a door and lifting a sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一线冷空气从门缝下钻进来，掀起一张纸。

branches.en: PLAIN FLOW: the general phrase and the local breeze differ only in scale.
branches.cn: 朴素流动：泛称与局地海风只在尺度上有别。

branches.en: VERTICAL PAIR: warm air climbs and cool air sinks, two halves of one loop.
branches.cn: 垂直成对：暖空气上升、冷空气下沉，是同一环流的两半。

branches.en: ROOM SCALE: a fan or a gap turns the same phrase into ventilation.
branches.cn: 房间尺度：风扇或缝隙把同一短语变成通风。

branches.en: SKY AND CABIN: high fast air steers weather and shakes aircraft.
branches.cn: 天空与机舱：高空快速气流既引导天气，也让飞机颠簸。

branches.en: SOCIAL FLOW: ideas move like air and carry people along.
branches.cn: 社会流动：思想像空气一样移动，并带动人群。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two independent words, each with its own suffix history: air is a borrowed root, and current is a Latin participle turned noun.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个独立单词构成，各有自己的后缀史：air 是借来的词根，current 是拉丁分词变成的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both halves: aer 'air' (itself from Greek) and currere 'to run', whose participle currens means 'running'.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都来自拉丁语：aer「空气」（本身来自希腊语）与 currere「跑」，其分词 currens 意为「奔跑的」。

items.example: The root also appears in cursor and excursion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 cursor 与 excursion 中。

items.meaningCN: 正在做或正在是，如「奔跑的」

items.example: The current carried the boat downstream.

items.meaning: the movement of air through a system

items.exampleCN: 气流受限会让发动机过热。

items.meaning: full of fresh air; light and open
items.example: The studio was bright and airy.
items.exampleCN: 这间工作室明亮又通风。

items.example: The cellar felt airless in summer.
items.exampleCN: 夏天这地窖闷得没有一丝风。

definition_zh: 压力大的；令人紧张的；消耗人的；要求过高的
definition_en: full of pressure or tension, and therefore tiring to deal with
core_image: 桌面上三份截止日期相同的文件，电话在响，咖啡已经凉透，椅背上还搭着没来得及穿的外套
scene: 凌晨的急诊值班室里，监护仪的滴答声没有停过，一名护士刚收拾完一张床位又被叫去下一张。 The stressful night shift left the nurses too tired to eat.
sceneCN: 这里 stressful 指「被压力占满、令人持续紧绷」（第 1 个义项：整体状态充满压力）；句意为这个压力极大的夜班让护士们累到吃不下东西。

pos.zh: 压力大的；令人紧张的；造成紧张的

derivatives.zh: 压力；紧张 / 强调；使紧张（拉丁词根「拉紧」，由拉紧转为压迫）
在充满压力的状态下（形容词加副词后缀）
压力程度（形容词加名词后缀，指性质本身）
压力源（动词加表施动者的后缀，指引起紧张的外在因素）

senses.title: Full of pressure
senses.definition: marked by heavy demands on time, attention or emotion, so that a person feels pressed
senses.definitionCN: 在时间、注意力或情绪上要求过重，使人感到被逼迫
senses.example: The stressful first year of teaching made him lose ten pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 教书第一年压力极大，他瘦了十磅。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'drawn tight', so a life with too many demands is a rope pulled past its slack.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「拉紧」，因此要求过多的生活就是一根被拉过余量的绳。

senses.title: Causing tension in a place
senses.definition: making a room, meeting or event tense for everyone present
senses.definitionCN: 使在场的每个人对某个场合感到紧张
senses.example: The stressful meeting ended with two colleagues refusing to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 那场令人紧张的会议以两名同事拒绝说话收场。
senses.why: Tension is not only inside one person; a setting can impose it on everyone who enters.
senses.whyCN: 紧张不只在一个人心里；一个场合也能把它压到每个进入其中的人身上。

senses.title: Physically taxing
senses.definition: demanding sustained physical effort, as of work or travel
senses.definitionCN: 需要持续体力付出的，如工作或旅途
senses.example: The stressful climb left the porters short of breath.
senses.exampleCN: 那段极耗体力的攀爬让脚夫们喘不上气。
senses.why: When the load is bodily rather than mental, the same pulling image describes muscles held at their limit.
senses.whyCN: 当负荷落在身体而非心上时，同一种拉扯的画面就用来形容被逼到极限的肌肉。

senses.title: Emotionally draining
senses.definition: using up emotional energy, so that a person is left flat and unable to respond
senses.definitionCN: 耗尽情绪能量，使人变得平淡、难以回应
senses.example: Caring for a sick relative for a year was far more stressful than she expected.
senses.exampleCN: 照护生病的亲人一年，远比她预想的更让人心力交瘁。
senses.why: Emotional labour also pulls: the effort is invisible, but the reserve is spent the same way.
senses.whyCN: 情绪劳动同样在拉扯：付出看不见，储备却以同样的方式被花掉。

senses.title: Demanding precision
senses.definition: requiring exact timing or accuracy, where a small slip matters
senses.definitionCN: 要求精确的时间或准确度，稍有偏差就有影响
senses.example: Landing the aircraft in crosswinds is a stressful task for any pilot.
senses.exampleCN: 侧风中降落对任何飞行员都是要求极高的任务。
senses.why: Precision adds a second rope: besides doing the work, one must not make a single error.
senses.whyCN: 精确再加一根绳：除了完成工作，还必须不出一个错。

senses.title: High-stakes
senses.definition: carrying consequences large enough that failure is costly
senses.definitionCN: 后果重大到一旦失败代价高昂
senses.example: The stressful entrance exam decides who gets the scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这场关系重大的入学考试决定谁拿到奖学金。
senses.why: The word turns into an assessment of stakes, not of effort: what matters is what a mistake would cost.
senses.whyCN: 这个词转为对利害的评估，而非对努力的评估：要紧的是犯错要付什么代价。

senses.title: Marked by conflict
senses.definition: full of disagreement or friction between people, so that contact itself is wearing
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间充满分歧与摩擦，以致接触本身就消耗人
senses.example: A stressful negotiation broke down twice before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一场冲突不断的谈判在黎明前破裂了两次。
senses.why: Conflict is tension made social: two ropes pulled in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是被社会化了的紧张：两根绳朝相反方向拉。

senses.title: Triggering a stress response
senses.definition: in research and medicine, describing a stimulus that raises the body's alarm response
senses.definitionCN: 在科研与医学中，形容引起身体警报反应的外在刺激
senses.example: Researchers measured cortisol after a stressful stimulus.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者在一段引发应激的刺激之后测量了皮质醇。
senses.why: The everyday word became a laboratory label once stress was studied as a bodily system.
senses.whyCN: 当压力被当作身体系统来研究，日常词就变成了实验室标签。

intro.en: Stressful is an English adjective built on stress plus the native ending -ful. Stress itself came through Old French from Latin, where the underlying verb meant 'to draw tight'.
intro.cn: stressful 是英语形容词，由 stress 加一个表示「充满」的本族形容词词尾构成。stress 本身经古法语来自拉丁语，其底层动词意为「拉紧」。

items.en: Stringere meant 'to draw tight, to graze, to touch lightly'. The tight-drawing sense is the one that survives in this family.
items.cn: stringere 意为「拉紧、擦过、轻触」。在这个词族里留下来的是「拉紧」这一义。

items.en: The past participle of the compound verb meant 'drawn apart, stretched, detained'. From it came the Old French noun for hardship and narrow straits.
items.cn: 那个复合动词的过去分词意为「被拉开、被拉伸、被扣住」。古法语中指困苦与窘迫的名词由它而来。

items.en: English took the Old French noun as a word for hardship, distress and, later, for emphasis laid on a syllable or an idea.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个古法语名词，用来指困苦、危难，后来又指落在音节或某个想法上的强调。

items.en: Engineers used the word for force per unit area, and physiologists borrowed it for the body's response to demand; the modern psychological sense dates from the twentieth century.
items.cn: 工程师用它指单位面积上的力，生理学家借它指身体对要求的反应；现代心理学义则始于 20 世纪。

items.en: The ending -ful is native English and means 'full of', so stressful simply says 'full of stress'.
items.cn: 那个形容词词尾是英语本族成分，意为「充满」，因此 stressful 直说就是「充满压力的」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of stringere is not settled, and the reconstructed Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：stringere 的更早来源没有定论，为它提出的印欧词根属重构，只是假说而非已证事实。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same tight-drawing family that are often confused with stressful; the second holds near neighbours that name difficulty in other terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拉紧」词族、常与 stressful 混淆的词；第二组是用其他方式指称艰难的近义词。

entries.definition: A doublet of stress, taken from the same Old French source: it means acute suffering or a situation of danger, not ongoing pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 与 stress 是同源双式词，来自同一个古法语来源：指剧烈痛苦或危险处境，而非持续压力。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb through a different French route: a strain is the pull itself, or the injury it causes.
entries.definitionCN: 经另一条法语路径来自同一个拉丁动词：strain 指拉力本身，或它造成的损伤。

entries.definition: Also from the drawing-tight verb, but it kept the sense of binding closely, hence rules enforced without slack.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自「拉紧」动词，但保留了「紧紧束缚」的意思，因此指不留余地的规则。

entries.definition: A derived word naming the cause rather than the experience: a stressor is what produces stress.
entries.definitionCN: 派生词，指成因而非体验：压力源是产生压力的东西。

entries.definition: It stresses the size of the demand; a demanding job may be satisfying rather than tense.
entries.definitionCN: 强调要求的份量；要求高的工作也可能令人满足，而不一定紧张。

entries.definition: It stresses depletion of energy, often physical, without the emotional charge of stressful.
entries.definitionCN: 强调精力的消耗，常指体力，不带 stressful 那样的情绪色彩。

entries.definition: It describes the mood of a room or a moment, and is also from the same drawing-tight root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容房间或时刻的气氛，也来自同一个「拉紧」词根。

entries.definition: A transparent compound rather than an established single word: it simply states that pressure is present.
entries.definitionCN: 透明的复合说法而非固定单词：只说明压力存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin base means 'drawn tight', and -ful means 'full of': a life pulled tight all round.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基意为「拉紧」，后面那个本族词尾意为「充满」：整个生活被拉得紧紧的。

normal.en: The family runs stress, stressful, stressfully, stressfulness, stressor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stress、stressful、stressfully、stressfulness、stressor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the setting: stressful job, stressful situation, stressful period.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：压力大的工作、紧张的处境、压力集中的时期。

normal.en: The same tight-drawing root gives strain, strict and distress.
normal.cn: 同一个「拉紧」词根衍生出 strain、strict 与 distress。

normal.en: Engineering uses the noun for force on an area; physiology uses it for the body's alarm.
normal.cn: 工程学用这个名词指单位面积上的力；生理学用它指身体的警报。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band around a stack of cards, one card too many.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈橡皮筋箍着一叠卡片，而卡片多了一张。

abstract.en: Picture a phone that rings every time you finally sit down.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电话，每次你终于坐下它就响。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge designed for ten trucks and carrying twelve.
abstract.cn: 想象一座按十辆卡车设计的桥，正载着十二辆。

examples.en: Many teachers describe the first term as the most stressful of their career.
examples.cn: 许多教师把第一个学期形容为职业生涯中压力最大的一段。

examples.en: Moving house is stressful even when everything goes well.
examples.cn: 即使一切顺利，搬家也是件让人紧张的事。

examples.en: The hospital reduced stressful noise at night to help patients sleep.
examples.cn: 医院减少了夜间令人紧张的噪音，以帮助病人入睡。

dict_mnemonic.text: stress（压力）+ ful（充满）＝ 从头到脚都是压力 → 压力大的、令人紧张的。

root: stress 经古法语来自拉丁 districtus「被拉开、被扣住」，底层是 stringere「拉紧」；后面那个本族词尾意为「充满」。同族有 strain、strict、distress、district。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rope: something is drawn tight. It can be a whole life, a room, a body on a climb, a spent heart, a task that allows no slip, a decision with high stakes, a fight, or a laboratory stimulus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一根绳展开：某物被拉紧。被拉紧的可以是一整段生活、一个房间、攀爬中的身体、被耗尽的心、不容失误的任务、代价重大的决定、一场争执，或实验室里的刺激。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope drawn past its slack until the fibres show.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拉过余量、纤维都露出来的绳。

branches.en: THE ROPE AND THE ROOM: a pressed life and the atmosphere it creates are the same pull seen from inside and outside.
branches.cn: 绳与房间：被逼迫的生活与它造出的气氛，是同一股拉力从内外两面看。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF COST: muscles at their limit and feelings spent to the bottom.
branches.cn: 两种代价：被逼到极限的肌肉，与被掏到底的情绪。

branches.en: A SECOND ROPE: precision adds the fear of one small slip on top of the work itself.
branches.cn: 第二根绳：精确在工作本身之上又加了一层对微小失误的恐惧。

branches.en: WHAT A MISTAKE COSTS: the word stops measuring effort and starts measuring stakes.
branches.cn: 错误的代价：这个词不再衡量付出，而开始衡量利害。

branches.en: PULLED FROM BOTH ENDS: conflict between people, and the body's own alarm when demand exceeds capacity.
branches.cn: 两端都在拉：人与人之间的冲突，以及要求超过承受时身体自身的警报。

intro.en: Stressful joins a Latin-derived noun to a native English ending, so it can be read as one borrowed part and one inherited part.
intro.cn: stressful 把一个源自拉丁语的名词接到一个英语本族词尾上，因此可以读成一半借来、一半继承。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb for drawing tight also builds the words for strain, strictness and distress, while the English ending marks 'full of'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「拉紧」的动词还构成指拉伤、严格与痛苦的一组词，而英语词尾表示「充满」。

items.exampleCN: 那艘船发出了求救信号。

intro.en: Departmental is department plus -al; department is depart plus -ment, from Latin partiri, to divide.
intro.cn: departmental 由 department 加 -al 构成；department 由 depart 加 -ment 构成，源自拉丁语 partiri（分开）。

items.en: Pars meant a part or share.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额。

items.en: Partiri meant to divide or share out.
items.cn: partiri 意为分开、分配。

items.en: Depart entered English for dividing and then leaving.
items.cn: 十五世纪 depart 先指分开，后指离开。

items.en: Department named a separate division of a whole.
items.cn: 十八世纪 department 指整体中分出的一个部分。

items.en: Departmental was formed as its adjective.
items.cn: 十九世纪 departmental 作为其形容词被造出。

items.en: It is standard in universities and government.
items.cn: 如今在大学与政府中是标准用语。

senses.whyCN: 名词 mate 命名同伴或配偶，动名词 mating 则命名作为一对结合起来的动作。

senses.title: The period of pairing
senses.definition: the season or stretch of time in which animals pair
senses.definitionCN: 动物配对的季节或一段时间
senses.example: Mating begins with the first warm rain.
senses.exampleCN: 交配随第一场暖雨开始。
senses.why: A gerund can name a time as well as an act, especially when the event is seasonal and predictable.
senses.whyCN: 动名词既能命名动作，也能命名时间，尤其当事件随季节发生且可预测时。

senses.title: The mating system of a species
senses.definition: the pattern a species follows in choosing and keeping partners, such as monogamy or polygyny
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种在选择与维持配偶上的模式，如一雄一雌或多雌
senses.example: The species has a mating system built on short pair bonds.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种的交配制度建立在短暂的配偶关系上。
senses.why: If pairing follows a pattern, the pattern can be named, and 'mating system' became the standard term for it.
senses.whyCN: 如果配对遵循某种模式，模式就能被命名，「交配制度」遂成为它的标准说法。

senses.title: A mating strategy
senses.definition: one of the alternative tactics an animal uses to obtain mates
senses.definitionCN: 动物为获得配偶而采用的替代策略之一
senses.example: Small males adopt a mating strategy that avoids the main arena.
senses.exampleCN: 体型小的雄性采取一种避开主战场的交配策略。
senses.why: Where partners are scarce, pairing becomes a problem with alternatives, and each alternative is called a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 当配偶稀缺时，配对就成了有替代方案的问题，每个方案便被称为一种策略。

senses.title: Breeding and cross-breeding
senses.definition: the controlled pairing of plants or animals by breeders
senses.definitionCN: 育种者有控制地把植物或动物配对
senses.example: The mating of the two lines produced a hardier grain.
senses.exampleCN: 两个品系的配种产生了更耐逆的谷物。
senses.why: Human breeders took the word from animal pairing and applied it to any controlled union of varieties.
senses.whyCN: 人类育种者从动物配对借来这个词，用于任何有控制的品种结合。

senses.title: Technical pairing of parts
senses.definition: the joining of two matching parts or devices into one assembly
senses.definitionCN: 把两个相配的零件或装置接成一个组件
senses.example: Check the mating of the connector before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 测试前检查接头的配合。
senses.why: The image of two things made to fit is old, and engineering reuses it for parts that must join exactly.
senses.whyCN: 两物被做成相合的形状，这个意象很古老，工程学把它复用于必须精确接合的零件。

senses.title: A temporary pair bond
senses.definition: the short association formed for one breeding attempt
senses.definitionCN: 为一次繁殖尝试而形成的短暂联结
senses.example: Their mating lasts a day; the eggs are left alone.
senses.exampleCN: 它们的配对只持续一天，卵被独自留下。
senses.why: Because mating is an event, it can also name the brief union that the event creates.
senses.whyCN: 因为交配是一个事件，它也能命名该事件造成的短暂结合。

senses.title: Abstract: any matched joining
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何成对的结合
senses.definition: any joining of two things that are made for each other
senses.definitionCN: 任何两个彼此相配之物的结合
senses.example: The mating of old brick and new glass defines the building.
senses.exampleCN: 旧砖与新玻璃的结合定义了这座建筑。
senses.why: At its widest, the word needs no animals: two things that fit together can be said to mate.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词不需要动物：两个彼此相合的东西也能被说成「结合」。

intro.en: Mating is the gerund of the verb mate, which came from the noun mate 'companion, spouse'. The noun is from Middle Low German mate, gemate 'one eating at the same table'.
intro.cn: mating 是动词 mate 的动名词，而 mate 来自名词 mate「同伴、配偶」。该名词来自中低地德语 mate、gemate「同桌吃饭的人」。

items.en: The compound meant '(one) having food together', from *ga- 'together' plus *matiz 'food'; the same *matiz gives English meat.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「共同有食物的人」，由 *ga-「共同」加 *matiz「食物」构成；同一个 *matiz 也给出英语 meat。

items.en: Middle Low German mate, gemate 'messmate, companion' entered English in the mid-fourteenth century as 'associate, fellow'.
items.cn: 中低地德语 mate、gemate「同餐伙伴、同伴」在 14 世纪中叶进入英语，义为「伙伴、同伴」。

items.en: By the 1540s mate named one of a married pair, and the animal sense of a partner followed from that.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 40 年代，mate 指已婚一对中的一方，动物配偶义由此引申。

items.en: The verb mate is recorded from about 1500 meaning 'to match or couple', and the animal sense 'to pair for breeding' from about 1600.
items.cn: 动词 mate 自约 1500 年有记录，意为「配对、结合」，其「为繁殖而配对」的动物义约自 1600 年出现。

items.en: Mating is the ordinary -ing form of that verb, and it became the standard biological noun in the twentieth century.
items.cn: mating 是该动词普通的 -ing 形式，到 20 世纪成为标准的生物学名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the reconstruction of *matiz and its Indo-European connections is debated, and the earliest citation of mating as a technical term is not fixed, so both should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*matiz 的重构及其印欧语联系存有争论；mating 作为术语的最早书证也无定论，因此两者都应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the verb, the person noun and a look-alike from the chess word; group two holds terms for the stages around mating.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词、表人名词与来自国际象棋的形近词；第二组是与交配相邻阶段的术语。

entries.definition: The noun and verb behind mating: a companion, a spouse, or to pair.
entries.definitionCN: mating 背后的名词与动词：同伴、配偶，或配对。

entries.definition: The past participle, used as an adjective for animals that have already paired.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，作形容词指已经配对的动物。

entries.definition: British informal for friendly, from mate 'companion'; it has nothing to do with breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「友好的」，来自 mate「同伴」；与繁殖无关。

entries.definition: From Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless', through Old French: it is not related to mate 'companion'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」，经古法语；与 mate「同伴」无关。

entries.definition: The whole process of producing offspring, including nesting and care; mating is one step in it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生后代的整个过程，包括筑巢与照料；mating 只是其中一步。

entries.definition: The forming of a pair, which may or may not involve reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形成一对，可能涉及繁殖，也可能不涉及。

entries.definition: The physical act of sexual union; mating also covers the whole pairing period and system.
entries.definitionCN: 性结合的身体动作；mating 还涵盖整个配对期与制度。

entries.definition: The displays that come before mating and often decide whether it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 交配之前的展示，常决定交配是否发生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mate + -ing: the act of pairing, taken from the verb.
normal.cn: mate + -ing：配对的动名词，来自动词。

normal.en: The family runs mate, mating, mated, matey, pairing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mate、mating、mated、matey、pairing。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mating season, mating system, mating behavior, mating success.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：交配季、交配制度、交配行为、交配成功率。

normal.en: Mate 'companion' came from a word for a person who shares food at table.
normal.cn: mate「同伴」来自指「同桌共食者」的词。

normal.en: Checkmate is from Persian, not from this family.
normal.cn: checkmate 来自波斯语，不属于这个词族。

abstract.cn: 想象两只蜻蜓在空中写下一个圆。

abstract.en: Picture two parts clicking together because they were cut to fit.
abstract.cn: 想象两个零件因被削成相合的形状而咔哒一声接上。

abstract.en: Picture old brick and new glass agreeing to hold one wall.
abstract.cn: 想象旧砖与新玻璃同意共撑一面墙。

examples.en: Mating peaks in the first weeks of the wet season.
examples.cn: 交配在雨季头几周达到高峰。

examples.en: The two lines were brought together for mating.
examples.cn: 两个品系被放在一起配种。

examples.en: Check the mating of the two surfaces before sealing.
examples.cn: 密封之前先检查两个面的配合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mate（配偶/配对）+ ing（进行中）」——正成对结合这件事 → 交配、配对

root: mate（中低地德语 mate/gemate「同餐伙伴」）+ -ing（古英语 -ung，表动作）；mate 的配偶义自 16 世纪 40 年代，动物配对义自约 1600 年；与 checkmate 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one event: the act of pairing, the season it fills, the system it follows, the strategy it uses, its use in breeding, its technical meaning, the short bond it creates, and finally any matched joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个事件：配对的动作、它占据的季节、它遵循的制度、它采用的策略、它在育种中的用途、它的技术义、它造成的短暂结合，最后是任何相合的结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two creatures or two parts coming together as one matched pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个生物或两个零件合成一对。

branches.en: ACT AND SEASON: the event itself, and the predictable time it fills.
branches.cn: 动作与季节：事件本身，以及它占据的可预测时间。

branches.en: PATTERN AND TACTIC: a species-wide system, and the individual alternatives within it.
branches.cn: 模式与战术：物种层面的制度，以及其中的个体替代方案。

branches.en: CONTROLLED BY PEOPLE: breeders take pairing in hand.
branches.cn: 被人控制：育种者把配对握在手中。

branches.en: PARTS AND BONDS: connectors that must fit, and pairs that last a day.
branches.cn: 零件与结合：必须相合的接头，以及只持续一天的配偶关系。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: anything made to go together.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何被做成相合之物。

intro.en: Mating is a Germanic noun plus the native suffix -ing; there is no Latin element in the word, and its Latin-looking neighbours belong to other families.
intro.cn: mating 是日耳曼语名词加本族后缀 -ing；词中没有拉丁成分，看似拉丁的近邻属于别的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source: mate is Germanic, and the suffix -ing is Old English -ung. Latin has no cognate family here, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁来源：mate 属日耳曼语，后缀 -ing 是古英语 -ung。此处没有拉丁同族词族，故不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 已配对的一对共用一巢。

definition_zh: 上升；攀登；爬坡；上坡路；（地位等的）提升
definition_en: the act of rising or climbing up, or an upward path or progress
core_image: 一条向上延伸的山路，登山者一步步往上走
scene: 清晨的薄雾中，登山队沿着结冰的山脊一步步向上攀。 The team began their ascent before sunrise to avoid the afternoon storm.
sceneCN: 这里 ascent 是「攀登、上升」（第 1 个义项：向上攀爬的动作）；句意是队伍日出前就开始攀登。

pos.zh: 上升；攀登
上坡路；提升

derivatives.zh: 同根动词（拉丁语 ascendere），义为「上升；攀登」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可攀登的」
由拉丁词干加后缀构成，义为「升天；升起」

senses.title: The act of climbing or rising
senses.definition: the action of moving upward, especially by climbing
senses.definitionCN: 向上移动的动作，尤指攀爬
senses.example: Their ascent of the north face took nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们攀登北壁用了九个小时。
senses.why: The Latin verb ascendere combines ad- (toward) with scandere (to climb), so an ascent is a going-up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ascendere 由 ad-（朝向）加 scandere（攀爬）构成，ascent 即「向上之行」。

senses.title: An upward path or slope
senses.definition: a way or slope that goes up, or the distance one climbs
senses.definitionCN: 向上的路径或斜坡，或爬升的高度
senses.example: The last part of the ascent is the steepest.
senses.exampleCN: 上坡的最后一段最陡。
senses.why: A physical climb leaves behind a physical track, so the word names the slope itself.
senses.whyCN: 攀爬会留下路径，因此该词也指坡道本身。

senses.title: Rise in status or power
senses.definition: progress upward in rank, influence, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在地位、影响力或重要性上的上升
senses.example: The film follows her ascent from intern to CEO.
senses.exampleCN: 影片讲述她从实习生到首席执行官的崛起。
senses.why: Upward movement works as a metaphor for social or career progress.
senses.whyCN: 向上移动被用作社会或职业进步的隐喻。

intro.en: Ascent comes from Latin ascendere (to climb up), formed of ad- toward plus scandere to climb.
intro.cn: ascent 源自拉丁语 ascendere（向上攀爬），由 ad-（朝向）+ scandere（攀爬）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *skand- means to leap or climb.
items.cn: 重构词根 *skand- 意为跳跃、攀爬。

items.en: Ascendere meant to climb up, from ad- plus scandere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ascendere 意为向上爬，由 ad- 加 scandere。

items.en: Old French ascente or ascencion carried the word into French usage.
items.cn: 古法语 ascente / ascencion 把该词带入法语。

items.en: English took ascent in the sixteenth century for both climbing and rising paths.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借用 ascent，兼指攀登与上坡路。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative rise in status.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了地位上升的比喻义。

note.en: Keep ascent (noun) distinct from assent (agreement); they sound the same but differ in root and sense.
note.cn: 注意 ascent（名词，攀登）与 assent（同意）同音异义，词根与意思都不同。

entries.definition: agreement or approval, a verb and noun of different Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 同意；赞成（同音异义词，词源不同）

entries.definition: to go up or climb

entries.definition: an upward journey on foot or by hand

entries.definition: a movement upward or an increase in position
entries.definitionCN: 上升；升起

entries.definition: height above a level

entries.definitionCN: 升级；加剧

entries.definition: a sloping path leading upward
entries.definitionCN: 上坡（路）

normalIntro.cn: 把 ascent 与 ascend 联系：去掉 d 加 t，就是「攀登」的名词。

normal.en: a- + scend echoes ad- + scandere, climb toward.
normal.cn: a- + scend 对应 ad- + scandere，即「向上爬」。

abstract.cn: 体会坡度变陡时加快的心跳。

abstract.en: See a career ladder fading into clouds above.
abstract.cn: 想象一架职业阶梯向上隐入云端。

examples.en: The ascent to the summit took the whole morning.
examples.cn: 登顶用了整个上午。

examples.en: His swift ascent in the company surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 他在公司里的迅速晋升让所有人吃惊。

examples.en: Cyclists dreaded the long ascent out of the valley.
examples.cn: 骑手们畏惧那段出谷的长上坡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额升」——额头向上升，正如 ascent 表示向上爬、攀升。

root: 源自拉丁语 ascendere（ad- 朝向 + scandere 攀爬），经古法语进入英语，指向上的动作与路径。

sensesIntro.en: From physical climbing the word widens to slopes and then to social rising.
sensesIntro.cn: 从具体的攀登出发，词义扩展到坡道，再比喻地位与权力的上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps tracing an upward slope
core.cn: 核心意象：脚步沿向上的坡道延伸

branches.en: the physical act of climbing
branches.cn: 具体的攀登动作

branches.en: the slope or route upward
branches.cn: 向上的坡道或路线

definition_zh: 电磁波谱；电磁辐射按波长（或频率）排列形成的完整谱段
definition_en: the full range of electromagnetic radiation, ordered by wavelength or frequency from radio waves to gamma rays
core_image: 一条从左到右由长波到短波渐变的彩色谱带，左端标着射电，右端标着伽马
scene: 夜里，射电望远镜的抛物面朝向天空，机房里一排屏幕显示着不同波段的信号曲线。 Radio telescopes read the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
sceneCN: 这里指电磁波谱中波长最长的那一段（第 4 个义项：射电与微波部分）；句意为射电望远镜读取的是电磁波谱的长波端。图中可辨识物件：抛物面天线、控制屏、信号曲线、夜空。

pos.zh: 名词短语：可数，指整个电磁波谱；也指某一具体波段范围

collocations.phrase: the visible part of the electromagnetic spectrum
collocations.zh: 电磁波谱中的可见部分
在整个电磁波谱范围内

collocations.phrase: the radio end of the electromagnetic spectrum
a band of the electromagnetic spectrum

derivatives.zh: 由表示「电的」与「磁的」两个成分构成，义为「电磁的」
本词第二成分的复数形式，义为「多个谱」
由本词第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「光谱的；谱的」

senses.title: The whole range of radiation
senses.definition: all electromagnetic radiation taken together, from the longest radio waves to the shortest gamma rays
senses.definitionCN: 从最长射电波到最短伽马射线的全部电磁辐射的总和
senses.example: The electromagnetic spectrum runs from radio waves to gamma rays without a gap.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱从射电波延伸到伽马射线，中间没有空隙。
senses.why: A single ordering by wavelength turns many apparently separate phenomena into one family.
senses.whyCN: 按波长排成一条序列，就把许多看似分离的现象归为同一族。

senses.title: Named bands
senses.definition: the conventional divisions of the spectrum into radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma bands
senses.definitionCN: 把波谱按惯例分为射电、微波、红外、可见光、紫外、伦琴射线与伽马等波段
senses.example: Astronomers divide the electromagnetic spectrum into bands named after their wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家按波长把电磁波谱分成若干波段。
senses.why: The bands are administrative and historical rather than sharply physical, but they let people talk about regions.
senses.whyCN: 这些分段更多是管理与历史形成的，而非物理上截然分明，但它们让人能谈论某些区域。

senses.title: The visible portion
senses.definition: the narrow band that the human eye can detect, roughly between violet and red
senses.definitionCN: 人眼能够感知的狭窄波段，大致介于紫光与红光之间
senses.example: The human eye samples only a narrow slice of the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 人眼只取用电磁波谱中很窄的一段。
senses.why: Sight is a narrow window, and the phrase makes that narrowness visible by contrast.
senses.whyCN: 视觉只是一扇窄窗，这个说法通过对比让这种狭窄变得可见。

senses.title: Radio and microwave portion
senses.definition: the long-wavelength end used by radio telescopes, radar and communication links
senses.definitionCN: 射电望远镜、雷达与通信链路所使用的长波段
senses.example: Radio telescopes read the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 射电望远镜读取的是电磁波谱的长波端。
senses.why: Long waves pass through dust and clouds, so this end of the spectrum reveals what optics cannot.
senses.whyCN: 长波能穿过尘埃与云层，因此波谱的这一端能揭示光学观测看不到的东西。

senses.title: Astronomical survey use
senses.definition: the practice of observing the same object in several bands to recover its full physical picture
senses.definitionCN: 在同一目标上观测多个波段，以还原其完整物理图景的做法
senses.example: Surveying the electromagnetic spectrum in many bands gives a fuller picture of a galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 在多个波段普查电磁波谱能给出更完整的星系图景。
senses.why: No single band tells the whole story, so astronomers stack observations across the spectrum.
senses.whyCN: 没有任何单一波段能讲完整个故事，因此天文学家把各波段观测叠在一起。

senses.title: Communication allocation
senses.definition: the regulated assignment of frequency ranges to operators and services
senses.definitionCN: 把频率范围按规定分配给运营商与业务的做法
senses.example: Regulators auction blocks of the electromagnetic spectrum to mobile operators.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构把电磁波谱中的若干频段拍卖给移动运营商。
senses.why: The spectrum is a finite public resource, so its use has to be divided by rules.
senses.whyCN: 波谱是有限的公共资源，其使用必须按规则划分。

senses.title: A plotted spectrum
senses.definition: a graph showing how much energy arrives at each wavelength or frequency
senses.definitionCN: 显示各波长或频率上到达多少能量的图
senses.example: A plot of the electromagnetic spectrum shows intensity against frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱的图示以频率为横轴显示强度。
senses.why: Once the range is drawn as a graph, peaks and gaps become readable at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把范围画成图，峰与空隙就能一眼读出。

senses.title: Spectral fingerprints
senses.definition: the pattern of absorption or emission lines by which a substance can be identified
senses.definitionCN: 可用来识别物质的吸收线或发射线图案
senses.example: Each element leaves a unique pattern in the electromagnetic spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 每种元素都在电磁波谱上留下独特的图案。
senses.why: Lines are element-specific, which turned the spectrum into a chemical fingerprint.
senses.whyCN: 谱线因元素而异，这就把波谱变成了化学指纹。

senses.title: The spectrum as a domain
senses.definition: the electromagnetic environment treated as a space to be controlled in communications and conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在通信与冲突中被视为需要掌控的电磁环境
senses.example: Modern forces plan to control the electromagnetic spectrum during a conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 现代军队计划在冲突中掌控电磁波谱。
senses.why: Military planners redefined a physical range as territory, which is a strategic rather than a scientific move.
senses.whyCN: 军事规划者把一段物理范围重新定义为「领土」，这是战略而非科学的操作。

intro.en: The phrase combines a nineteenth-century adjective for electricity and magnetism with a Latin word that Newton had already used for the band of prismatic colours. The pieces are well documented; the exact date of the full phrase is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把十九世纪表示电与磁的形容词，与一个已被牛顿用来指棱镜色带的拉丁词组合起来。各部分来源有据，整个短语的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, because rubbing amber produces static charge.
items.cn: 这个词指琥珀，因为摩擦琥珀会产生静电。

items.en: Magnes named the lodestone of Magnesia, the original natural magnet.
items.cn: 这个词指马格尼西亚的磁石，即最早被认识的天然磁体。

items.en: Spectrum meant an appearance or image, from the verb meaning to look.
items.cn: 这个词表示外观或影像，来自表示「看」的动词。

items.en: Newton used spectrum for the coloured band thrown by a prism, fixing the word in optics.
items.cn: 牛顿用这个词指棱镜投出的彩色带，使其在光学中定型。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics showed that electricity, magnetism and light are one phenomenon.
items.cn: 十九世纪的物理学证明电、磁与光是同一种现象。

items.en: The full phrase appears once the whole range of radiation was understood as a single ordered set, late in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 当全部辐射被理解为一条有序序列后，完整短语才出现，时在十九世纪晚期。

note.en: The first group shares the adjective or the noun spectrum; the second group names particular bands and kinds of range.
note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「电磁的」或名词「谱」；第二组指特定波段与范围类型。

entries.definition: Energy carried by oscillating electric and magnetic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 由振荡电场与磁场携带的能量。

entries.definition: A wave of coupled electric and magnetic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 电场与磁场相互耦合形成的波。

entries.definition: The field produced by charges and currents.
entries.definitionCN: 由电荷与电流产生的场。

entries.definition: A range of wavelengths or frequencies.
entries.definitionCN: 一段波长或频率范围。

entries.definition: Relating to a spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 与谱相关的。

entries.definition: The band of light the eye can see.
entries.definitionCN: 人眼能看见的那段光。

entries.definition: The frequencies used for radio communication.
entries.definitionCN: 用于无线电通信的频率范围。

entries.definition: A continuous range of frequencies set aside for a use.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途划出的一段连续频率。

entries.definition: The span between the shortest and longest waves observed.
entries.definitionCN: 所观测最短波与最长波之间的跨度。

entries.definition: The extent of wavelengths an instrument can record.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器能记录的波长范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the rainbow strip outward in both directions; abstract ones treat the spectrum as a single ordered map of one phenomenon.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着彩虹色带向两端延伸；抽象联想把波谱看作同一现象的一张有序地图。

normal.en: Prism in, rainbow out: that band is the visible part.
normal.cn: 棱镜进去，彩虹出来，那条色带就是可见部分。

normal.en: Stretch the rainbow far left and you reach radio waves.
normal.cn: 把彩虹向左拉得很远，就到了射电波。

normal.en: Stretch it far right and you reach gamma rays.
normal.cn: 向右拉得很远，就到了伽马射线。

normal.en: Radio telescopes work at the long-wave end where dust cannot block them.
normal.cn: 射电望远镜工作在尘埃挡不住的长波端。

normal.en: Every element writes its own lines on the strip.
normal.cn: 每种元素都在这条带上写下自己的谱线。

abstract.en: The spectrum is one axis: everything electromagnetic is a position on it.
abstract.cn: 波谱就是一根轴：一切电磁现象都是它上面的一个位置。

abstract.en: Bands are habits of speech, not walls in nature.
abstract.cn: 波段是说话的习惯，不是自然界的墙。

abstract.en: A resource becomes territory the moment someone writes rules for it.
abstract.cn: 资源一旦被人写下规则，就变成了领土。

examples.en: Visible light occupies only a small part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 可见光只占电磁波谱的一小部分。

examples.en: The satellite monitors several bands of the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星监测电磁波谱的若干波段。

examples.en: Engineers test how the material responds across the electromagnetic spectrum.
examples.cn: 工程师测试该材料在整个电磁波谱上的响应。

dict_mnemonic.text: electromagnetic（电磁的）+ spectrum（谱）——电磁的谱，即电磁波谱

root: 由 electromagnetic 与 spectrum 组合。前者由希腊语 elektron「琥珀」与拉丁语 magnes「磁石」经 magnet 构成；后者来自拉丁语 spectrum「外观、影像」，出自表示「看」的动词。牛顿先以该词指棱镜色带，十九世纪晚期辐射被理解为一条有序序列后，完整短语才定型，确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses unroll one ordered strip: its whole length, its bands, its visible slice, its long-wave end, its uses, its regulation, its graphs, its lines and its strategic reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项展开同一条有序谱带：全长、分段、可见的一小段、长波端、用途、管理、图示、谱线与其战略解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip that shifts from long red waves to short violet ones, then keeps going both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条由长波红端过渡到短波紫端的谱带，并向两端继续延伸。

branches.en: THE CORE TWO: one continuous range and the conventional bands cut into it.
branches.cn: 核心两项：一条连续范围，以及在其上划分的惯用波段。

branches.en: THE TWO ENDS PEOPLE USE: the narrow visible slice and the long-wave end.
branches.cn: 人常用的两端：狭窄的可见段与长波段。

branches.en: THE USES: multi-band astronomy and regulated communication blocks.
branches.cn: 用途：多波段天文观测与受管制的通信频段。

branches.en: THE READINGS: intensity plotted against frequency, and lines that identify elements.
branches.cn: 读法：以频率为横轴画强度，以及可识别元素的谱线。

branches.en: THE STRATEGIC SHIFT: the same strip treated as a domain to control.
branches.cn: 战略转向：同一条谱带被当作需要掌控的领域。

intro.en: Two Greek and Latin roots plus a Latin noun of appearance make up the phrase, and its second element has generated a large family.
intro.cn: 两个希腊与拉丁词根加一个表示外观的拉丁名词构成了这个短语，其第二成分还衍生出一大族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies the word for amber, Latin supplies the lodestone and the noun for appearance; modern science combined them.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「琥珀」一词，拉丁语提供了「磁石」与表示外观的名词；近代科学把它们组合起来。

items.example: The word gave its name to electricity because amber holds charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词因琥珀能带电荷而成为「电」的名称来源。

items.example: It named the natural magnet found in one district.
items.exampleCN: 它指在某一地区发现的天然磁体。

items.example: Newton fixed its optical sense as the band of colours.
items.exampleCN: 牛顿把它的光学含义固定为彩色带。

items.example: The noun is built on the act of looking.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词建立在「看」这一动作上。

items.example: It marks the electrical half of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它标记形容词中「电」的那一半。

items.example: It turns the noun magnet into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词「磁体」变成形容词。

items.example: The ending appears in the Latin noun for a means of seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾出现在拉丁语中表示「观看手段」的名词里。

items.example: The adjective describes anything belonging to a spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述属于谱的事物。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「电的」与「磁的」两个成分构成，义为「电磁的」
本词第二成分的复数形式，义为「多个谱」
由本词第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「光谱的；谱的」
由本词第二成分加表示「观测、研究」的成分构成，义为「光谱学」
由本词第二成分加表示「观察仪器」的成分构成，义为「分光镜」
由本词第二成分加表示「测量仪器」的成分构成，义为「光谱仪」

definition_zh: 适应；使适应；改编；调整以适合；改装
definition_en: to change or be changed so as to fit new conditions, a new medium or a new purpose
core_image: 苗圃里一排幼苗从温室搬到露天，头几天盖着遮阳网，叶片慢慢转向新的光照
scene: 苗圃把温室里的幼苗搬到露天，头几天盖着遮阳网，叶片慢慢转向新的光照。 Young plants can adapt to stronger light within a week.
sceneCN: 这里指生物对新光照条件逐渐适应（第 1 个义项：适应环境气候）；句意为幼苗能在一周内适应更强的光照。图中可辨识物件：幼苗、遮阳网、温室门。

pos.zh: 适应；使适应；改编；调整

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加名词尾构成，义为「适应；改编作品」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「能适应的；可改编的」
由该形容词加名词尾构成，义为「适应性；可改编性」
由该动词加表示器具或施动者的名词尾构成，义为「适配器；改编者」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「适应的；有适应性的」

senses.title: To suit a climate or habitat
senses.definition: to become suited to the temperature, light, water or other conditions of a place
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐适合某地的温度、光照、水分或其他条件
senses.example: Polar plants can adapt to extreme cold.
senses.exampleCN: 极地植物能够适应极度寒冷。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fit, and the first thing a living thing must fit is the place it lives in.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使合适，而生物首先要合适的就是它所居住的地方。

senses.title: To adjust to a new situation
senses.definition: to change one's habits or expectations so as to work within new circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 改变习惯或预期，以便在新环境中运转
senses.example: The staff will adapt to the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 员工将会适应新的时间表。
senses.why: Once fitting is applied to human arrangements, it covers shifts in work, rules and daily rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「使合适」用于人的安排，就涵盖了工作、规则与日常节奏的变化。

senses.title: To make something fit
senses.definition: to alter a person or thing so that it fits a requirement or a group
senses.definitionCN: 改变人或事物，使其符合某项要求或某一群体
senses.example: A good teacher can adapt to mixed abilities in one class.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师能够适应一个班里参差不齐的能力。
senses.why: The verb is transitive in Latin, so English can put the thing being fitted either as its object or behind the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在拉丁语里是及物的，因此英语既可把被调整之物放在宾语位置，也可放在短语之后。

senses.title: To adapt a work for another medium
senses.titleCN: 把作品改编成另一形式
senses.definition: to change a story, play or piece of music so that it can be presented in a different medium or for a different audience
senses.definitionCN: 改动故事、戏剧或音乐，使其能以另一种媒介呈现或面向另一批受众
senses.example: The studio can adapt to television by splitting the novel into six parts.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方可以把这部小说拆成六集，以改编成电视作品。
senses.why: A work must fit a new stage, screen or page, and the word for fitting became the word for rewriting.
senses.whyCN: 作品必须适合新的舞台、银幕或版面，于是「使适合」这个词变成了「改编」。

senses.title: To adjust a plan so that it fits
senses.definition: to change a plan, budget or design so that it meets a limit or a need
senses.definitionCN: 改动计划、预算或设计，使其符合某项限制或需求
senses.example: We can adapt to a smaller budget by cutting travel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以削减差旅，以调整方案适应更小的预算。
senses.why: Planning repeats the same fit: means are trimmed until they match the available resources.
senses.whyCN: 规划重复着同一个「合适」：手段被削减，直到与可用资源相配。

senses.title: To adjust bodily to a stimulus
senses.definition: to undergo a bodily change that reduces the response to a repeated stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 身体发生变化，使对重复刺激的反应减弱
senses.example: Eyes can adapt to dim light after a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛几分钟后就能适应昏暗的光线。
senses.why: The body fits itself to its surroundings without conscious design, and physiology kept the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 身体无需有意的设计就能使自己适合环境，生理学沿用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To conform to customs and rules
senses.definition: to change one's behaviour so that it agrees with the customs or expectations of a group
senses.definitionCN: 改变自身行为，使其与某群体的习俗或期待相符
senses.example: Newcomers may adapt to local customs within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新来者可能一年之内就顺应了当地习俗。
senses.why: Social life asks people to fit a pattern, and the verb covers that quiet conformity as well as physical change.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活要求人符合某种模式，这个动词既指身体变化，也指这种不声张的顺应。

senses.title: To modify equipment for a new use
senses.titleCN: 改装设备以适应新用途
senses.definition: to change a device or machine so that it works with new parts, fuel or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改动装置或机器，使其能配合新的零件、燃料或条件
senses.example: The workshop can adapt to metric parts by machining new fittings.
senses.exampleCN: 车间可以加工新的接头，使设备适应公制零件。
senses.why: Tools are fitted to tasks, and a machine altered for a new task is literally made suitable.
senses.whyCN: 工具要被适合任务，为新技术任务而改动的机器正是字面意义上的「被使合适」。

intro.en: Adapt comes from Latin adaptare, to fit something to something, from ad-, to or towards, and aptare, to make fit, from aptus, fit or fastened. English took the verb in the seventeenth century, and the phrase adapt to followed the verb's own construction.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「adaptare」「使某物适合某物」，由「ad-」「朝向」和「aptare」「使合适」构成，而「aptare」又出自「aptus」「合适的、系紧的」。英语在十七世纪引入这个动词，短语「adapt to」沿用了动词本身的搭配。

items.en: The adjective meant fit, suitable and also fastened, so fitness and attachment were one idea.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合适的、适宜的，也有系紧之意，因此「合适」与「连接」是同一个概念。

items.en: The verb meant to make fit or to fasten, and it gave the action of putting a thing into its proper place.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使合适或系紧，给出了把事物放到恰当位置的动作。

items.en: The prefix meant towards, and it turned the fitting into a movement towards a particular condition.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为朝向，把「使合适」变成了朝某一特定条件靠拢的动作。

items.en: The compound meant to fit one thing to another, and it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为使一事物适合另一事物，是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the seventeenth century for fitting, and soon for rewriting a work for a new medium.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词表示使适合，很快又用于把作品改写以适合新媒介。

items.en: The preposition to marks the condition or purpose that is being fitted, and the phrase became fixed in ordinary and technical English.
items.cn: 介词「to」标出所适合的条件或目的，这个短语在普通英语与技术英语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that look or sound like adapt; the second group gathers verbs of fitting and changing.
note.cn: 第一组收录在形音上与「adapt」相近的形式；第二组收录表示使适合与改变的说法。

entries.definition: To fit or be fitted to new conditions; the base verb of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指使适合或被适合新条件；是该短语的基础动词。

entries.definition: The process or result of fitting, including a work rewritten for a new medium.
entries.definitionCN: 指适合的过程或结果，也包括为新媒介改写的作品。

entries.definition: Able to be changed so as to fit different conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被改变以适合不同条件的。

entries.definition: To take a child or an idea as one's own; it looks close but its Latin verb means to choose.
entries.definitionCN: 指收养孩子或采纳想法；形近但其拉丁动词意为选择。

entries.definition: Highly skilled at something; it looks close but comes from a Latin word for having attained.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某事上非常熟练；形近但出自拉丁语表示「已达到」的词。

entries.definition: To change something slightly so that it works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 指稍作改动使某物运作更好或更合适。

entries.definition: To change in order to meet the needs of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为满足某人或某物的需要而作出改变。

entries.definition: To become used to a new climate or environment over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指随着时间逐渐习惯新的气候或环境。

entries.definition: To change something, often to improve it or give it a new purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指改动某物，常为改进或赋予新用途。

entries.definition: To make or change something so that it suits a particular person or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作或改动某物，使其适合特定的人或目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin sense of fitting, the real family of the verb, and the real phrases of climate, work and equipment.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「使合适」之义、这个动词的真实词族，以及气候、工作与设备的真实搭配。

normal.en: Aptus meant fit and fastened, so adapt began as the act of putting a thing where it belongs.
normal.cn: 「aptus」意为合适的、系紧的，因此「adapt」最初就是把事物放到它该在的位置。

normal.en: Adapt, adapter, adaptation and adaptable all carry the same idea of fitting.
normal.cn: 「adapt」「adapter」「adaptation」与「adaptable」都带着同一个「使合适」的意思。

normal.en: The phrase adapt to always needs a target: a climate, a timetable, a budget or a medium.
normal.cn: 短语「adapt to」总需要一个目标：气候、时间表、预算或媒介。

normal.en: An adapter is a small piece that makes one plug fit another socket, the word's meaning made visible.
normal.cn: 适配器是一个让小插头适合另一插座的小物件，正是这个词的意思变得可见。

normal.en: Eyes adapt to dim light, workers adapt to new rules, and both are the same quiet fitting.
normal.cn: 眼睛适应暗光，员工适应新规，两者都是同一种不声张的适合。

abstract.en: To adapt is to keep one's aim while changing one's shape, like water taking the shape of its cup.
abstract.cn: 适应就是保持目的而改变形状，像水取杯子的形状。

abstract.en: A species and a story survive by the same move: the form bends so that the core may continue.
abstract.cn: 物种与故事靠同一个动作存活：外形弯一弯，核心才能继续。

abstract.en: The deepest adaptation is invisible: the change has finished before anyone notices that it was needed.
abstract.cn: 最深的适应是看不见的：变化在别人察觉需要之前就已经完成。

examples.en: Desert animals can adapt to heat by resting in shade.
examples.cn: 沙漠动物可以通过在阴凉处休息来适应炎热。

examples.en: The director will adapt to a smaller stage by cutting two scenes.
examples.cn: 导演会删去两场戏，以适应更小的舞台。

examples.en: Older workers may adapt to the software after a short course.
examples.cn: 年长员工上完短期课程后可能就适应这款软件了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿达普特·图」——把自己调到合适的位置：适应、改编、改装

root: 拉丁语「adaptare」「使适合」=「ad-」「朝向」+「aptare」「使合适」←「aptus」「合适的、系紧的」；英语十七世纪引入，短语沿用动词自身搭配。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend the idea of fitting: fitting a climate, fitting a new situation, fitting another person, fitting a work to a medium, fitting a plan to a limit, fitting the body to a stimulus, fitting behaviour to custom, and fitting a machine to new parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项延伸「使合适」这一观念：适合气候、适合新情况、使他人适合、把作品改为另一媒介、让计划适合限制、身体适应刺激、行为顺应习俗、设备配合新零件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seedling is moved into stronger light, and its leaves turn until they face the new source.
core.cn: 核心意象：幼苗被移到更强的光下，叶片转动，直到朝向新的光源。

branches.en: THE LIVING FIT: a plant or a person settles into a climate and a new daily arrangement.
branches.cn: 生命的适合：植物或人安顿进一种气候与新的日常安排。

branches.en: THE DELIBERATE FIT: a teacher or a planner alters means until a requirement is met.
branches.cn: 有意的适合：教师或规划者调整手段，直到满足要求。

branches.en: THE WORK IN A NEW MEDIUM: a story is reshaped for stage, screen or page.
branches.cn: 新媒介中的作品：故事为舞台、银幕或版面重新塑形。

branches.en: THE BODY'S QUIET FIT: the senses dull their response to a repeated stimulus.
branches.cn: 身体的静默适合：感官对重复刺激的反应逐渐减弱。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND MECHANICAL FIT: behaviour follows custom, and a machine takes new parts.
branches.cn: 社会与机械的适合：行为随习俗调整，机器换上新的零件。

intro.en: Adapt is a Latin verb of fitting, and its family covers both the living and the mechanical sides of the idea.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「使合适」的拉丁动词，其词族涵盖这一观念的生物与机械两面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies aptus, aptare and adaptare; the adjective aptus is the seed of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「aptus」、「aptare」与「adaptare」；形容词「aptus」是整个词族的种子。

intro.en: Enhancer is enhance plus the agent ending -er; enhance reaches English through Old French enhaucier, from Vulgar Latin altiare, to make high, so an enhancer is the thing that lifts a quality higher.
intro.cn: enhancer 由 enhance 加表示施事者的 -er 构成；enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），所以 enhancer 就是把某种品质往上抬的那个东西。

items.en: Altus means high in Latin and gives altitude.
items.cn: altus 在拉丁语中意为高，给出 altitude。

items.en: Altiare is the spoken Latin verb meaning to make high.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语 altiare 是意为抬高的口语动词。

items.en: Enhaucier means to raise or exalt in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语 enhaucier 意为举起、抬高。

items.en: Enhance enters English for raising value or degree.
items.cn: 15 世纪 enhance 进入英语，指提高价值或程度。

items.en: The agent noun appears with industrial and chemical uses.
items.cn: 19 世纪出现带工业与化学用途的施事名词。

items.en: Software options for images adopt the same word.
items.cn: 21 世纪处理图像的软件选项也沿用该词。

note.en: Enhancer, enhance and enhancement share the same verb; heighten and amplifier carry the sense from other roots, while -er here marks the thing that does the work.
note.cn: enhancer、enhance 与 enhancement 共用同一个动词；heighten 与 amplifier 从别的词根表达相近意思，而这里的 -er 指做出该动作的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: enhancer ＝ enhance（提高）＋ -er（做这件事的东西）＝「增强器；增强剂」。动词 enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），词根是意为高的 altus。名词 enhancement 是结果，enhancer 是手段。三类用法：设备 a signal enhancer 信号增强器、配料 a flavour enhancer 增味剂、软件 an image enhancer 图像增强器。复数 enhancers 指多种或几件增强装置。

root: 拉丁语 altus（高的）→ 俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高）→ enhance（提高）＋ -er → enhancer（增强器；增强剂）

definition_en: to gather material together into a book, list or file; to translate source code into machine instructions
core_image: 一摞散页被按页码收进同一只硬壳夹
scene: 编辑桌上摊着几十封信，她把它们按年份装进同一册。 She spent a year compiling letters into a single volume.
sceneCN: 这里指把零散材料收集整理成一部作品（第 1 个义项：汇编成书）；句意是她花一年时间把信件汇编成一册。

senses.title: To gather material into a book
senses.definition: to collect scattered writings and arrange them into one work
senses.definitionCN: 收集零散文字并编排成一部作品
senses.example: She compiled the letters into a single volume.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这些信件汇编成一册。
senses.why: Latin compilare meant to gather together, and book-making gave the gathering a finished shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 compilare 意为聚拢，制书让这种聚拢有了完成形态。

senses.title: To make a list
senses.definition: to draw up items in an ordered list
senses.definitionCN: 把条目按次序列成清单
senses.example: He compiled a list of every address in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了一份全区地址清单。
senses.why: A list is the smallest finished form that gathering can take.
senses.whyCN: 清单是「聚拢」能取得的最小完成形态。

senses.title: To assemble data for use
senses.definition: to collect figures from many sources into one set
senses.definitionCN: 把多处数字汇集为一套
senses.example: The office compiled the figures before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室在会前汇总了这些数字。
senses.why: Modern administration gathers first and decides later.
senses.whyCN: 现代行政先汇集，后决定。

senses.title: To translate source code
senses.definition: to turn a program written by a person into instructions a machine can run
senses.definitionCN: 把人类写的程序转成机器能执行的指令
senses.example: The compiler turns each source file into an object file.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器把每个源文件转成目标文件。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the gathering word for a one-way translation into machine form.
senses.whyCN: 计算技术借这个「汇集」词，指单向转成机器形式。

senses.title: To collect evidence
senses.definition: to bring together documents and facts for an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为论证把文件与事实聚在一起
senses.example: The lawyer compiled the records into one file.
senses.exampleCN: 律师把这些记录汇入一个卷宗。
senses.why: The old sense of gathering without order survives in this use.
senses.whyCN: 古老的无序聚拢义在这种用法里仍然活着。

senses.title: To build an index or catalogue
senses.definition: to arrange entries so that each can be found
senses.definitionCN: 把条目编排到每一条都可查到
senses.example: The librarian compiled an index of the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 馆员为这批藏书编了索引。
senses.why: Order is added to the gathering, and the result is a finding tool.
senses.whyCN: 聚拢之上加了次序，结果就是检索工具。

senses.title: To draw up a report
senses.definition: to put gathered facts into a formal written account
senses.definitionCN: 把汇集的事实写成正式叙述
senses.example: The team compiled a report on the flood damage.
senses.exampleCN: 团队编写了一份洪灾损失报告。
senses.why: The word moves from collecting to composing without leaving the desk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从收集走到撰写，始终没有离开书桌。

senses.title: To make an anthology
senses.definition: to choose pieces and arrange them as a collection
senses.definitionCN: 挑选篇目并编排成集
senses.example: The editor compiled an anthology of river poems.
senses.exampleCN: 编者编了一部河流诗选。
senses.why: Selection and arrangement are the two halves of compiling.
senses.whyCN: 挑选与编排是「编」的两半。

intro.en: Compile comes from Latin compilare, to gather together, perhaps also to plunder, from com- together plus pilare. The direct source is clear; the meaning of pilare in this compound is source uncertain.
intro.cn: compile 来自拉丁 compilare「聚拢」，也可能带「掠夺」义，由 com-「一起」与 pilare 构成。直接来源清楚；pilare 在这个复合词中的含义来源不确定。

items.en: Compilare meant to plunder, to gather together and to heap up, with the idea of things brought into one place.
items.cn: compilare 意为掠夺、聚拢、堆起，核心是把东西弄到一处。

items.en: Com- means together, and it supplies the collecting force of the verb.
items.cn: com- 意为一起，提供这个动词的收集力量。

items.en: Pilare is connected with pressing or plucking, but which of those senses belongs to this compound is source uncertain.
items.cn: pilare 与压、拔相关，但在此复合词中取哪一义，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French compiler narrowed the word to the gathering of writings.
items.cn: 古法语 compiler 把词义收窄到文字的汇集。

items.en: English took the verb in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: In the 1950s the word was given to the translation of source code, which gathers programmes into machine form.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代，这个词被用于源代码翻译，即把程序汇集为机器形式。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin gathering stem; the second group names collecting and arranging.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「聚拢」词干；第二组是收集与编排的近义说法。

normal.en: Compilare is to gather together, and the book is the gathered thing made visible.
normal.cn: compilare 是聚拢，而书就是让聚拢之物显现的形态。

normal.en: Compiler is the person and, later, the program that gathers code into machine form.
normal.cn: compiler 先是编纂的人，后来是汇集代码为机器形式的程序。

normal.en: Comply looks close but comes from filling, not from gathering.
normal.cn: comply 形近，却出自「填满」，不是「聚拢」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: compile a dictionary, compile a list, compile source code.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：编纂词典、编制清单、编译源代码。

normal.en: An anthology is a compiled book, chosen and arranged.
normal.cn: 选集就是编成的书，经过挑选与编排。

abstract.en: Compile is a table covered with loose pages, finally sorted into one binder.
abstract.cn: 汇编是一张摊满散页的桌子，最后被理进同一只夹子。

abstract.en: The act is half gathering and half order; without the second half it is only a pile.
abstract.cn: 这项行为一半是收集，一半是编排；少了后一半，就只是一堆。

abstract.en: A compiler translates a human arrangement into a machine's arrangement.
abstract.cn: 编译器把人的编排翻译成机器的编排。

examples.en: The archivist compiled the letters by year and by sender.
examples.cn: 档案员按年份与寄信人汇编这些信件。

examples.en: The program compiles the whole project in under a second.
examples.cn: 这个程序在一秒之内编译整个项目。

examples.en: She compiled a short list of the books worth keeping.
examples.cn: 她编了一份值得保留的短书单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯派尔」——把一堆散页肯（肯）定派进同一册：汇编

root: 拉丁 compilare「聚拢、堆起」，也可能带「掠夺」义 ← com-「一起」+ pilare（与压、拔相关，此复合词中取义来源不确定）。古法语 compiler 把义收窄到文字汇集；英语中世纪晚期借入，确切首见年代不确定。同族 compilation、compiler；comply 形近但出自 complere「填满」。二十世纪五十年代起又指源代码编译。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses gather writings, list items, assemble data, translate code, collect evidence, build indexes, draft reports and choose an anthology.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分别汇集文字、列清单、汇总数据、编译代码、汇集证据、编索引、写报告与编选集。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose pages gathered from a table into one hard binder.
core.cn: 核心意象：散页从桌面上被收进同一只硬壳夹。

branches.en: THE FINISHED VOLUME: scattered writings made into a book and chosen pieces made into an anthology.
branches.cn: 成书：散落文字编成书，挑选篇目编成选集。

branches.en: THE FINDING FORM: an ordered list and an index built to be searched.
branches.cn: 检索形态：按序的清单与供查找的索引。

branches.en: THE GATHERED MATERIAL: figures from many sources and records for an argument.
branches.cn: 汇集的材料：多处数字与供论证的记录。

branches.en: THE MACHINE TRANSLATION: source code turned into instructions.
branches.cn: 机器翻译：源代码转成指令。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN ACCOUNT: gathered facts set down as a report.
branches.cn: 成文的叙述：汇集的事实写成报告。

intro.en: Compile is the Latin verb compilare with English noun and agent forms; com- is clear and the other element is disputed.
intro.cn: compile 是拉丁动词 compilare 加英语名词与施动形式；com- 清楚，另一成分有争议。

latinIntro.en: Com- supplies the gathering, pilare supplies the disputed action, and compilatio supplies the noun.
latinIntro.cn: com- 提供「聚拢」，pilare 提供有争议的动作，compilatio 提供名词。

items.example: The prefix brings scattered things into one place.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把散落之物带到一处。

items.example: The element is the disputed part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这一成分是复合词中有争议的部分。

items.example: The verb already carried both collection and seizure.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词已兼有收集与夺取。

items.example: The noun names the finished gathering.

items.meaning: to gather writings; one who gathers
items.example: French narrowed the verb to writings before English took it.
items.exampleCN: 法语先把动词收窄到文字，再传给英语。

items.example: English keeps the book-making sense at the centre.
items.exampleCN: 英语把制书义留在中心。

items.example: The noun can name the book or the act.
items.exampleCN: 名词既可指书，也可指行为。

items.example: The participle marks the finished state.
Computing reused the agent word for a machine.
items.exampleCN: 计算技术把施动名词复用给了机器。

items.example: It also builds compilation, foundation and creation.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 compilation、foundation 与 creation。
