definition_zh: 审计师；查账员；稽核员；（大学）旁听生；（古义）听者
definition_en: a person whose job is to examine accounts or to check that rules are followed; in American universities, a student who attends a class without credit; formerly, a listener
core_image: 外人坐在长桌对面，逐笔听账、逐笔打钩
scene: 事务所派来的人翻开凭证，一笔一笔问到深夜。 The auditor asked for every receipt from the last quarter.
sceneCN: 这里 auditor 是「审计师、查账员」（第 1 个义项）；句意是审计师索要上一季度的每一张收据。

pos.zh: 名词：审计师；稽核员；旁听生；听者

derivatives.zh: 同族基础词：审计；查账
同族动名词：审计工作
同族形容词：可审计的
加「职位」后缀：审计师的职位

senses.title: A professional examiner of accounts
senses.definition: a qualified person whose job is to examine financial records and report on them
senses.definitionCN: 以检查财务记录并出具报告为职业的专业人员
senses.example: The auditor signed the report without qualification.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师无保留地签署了报告。
senses.why: Latin auditor meant a hearer, and accounts were once read aloud to him, so the job title still carries the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里这个词意为「听的人」，账目从前是念给他听的，所以这个职称至今仍带着耳朵。

senses.title: An inspector of rules and systems
senses.definition: a person who checks that an organization follows rules, standards or its own procedures
senses.definitionCN: 检查某机构是否遵守规则、标准或自身流程的人
senses.example: A quality auditor visited the plant twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 质量稽核员每年到厂两次。
senses.why: The listening role generalized: what is checked need not be money, only something that must match a rule.
senses.whyCN: 「听审」的角色被推广：被检查的不必是钱款，只要是必须与规则相符的东西即可。

senses.title: A student listening without credit
senses.definition: a student who attends a university course without taking examinations or earning credit
senses.definitionCN: 在大学听课但不参加考试、不取学分的学生
senses.example: The professor welcomed auditors to the back rows.
senses.exampleCN: 教授欢迎旁听生坐到后排。
senses.why: American usage returned to the literal Latin sense: a person who hears, and nothing more.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法回到了拉丁语的字面义：一个听的人，仅此而已。

senses.title: A hearer in older English
senses.definition: in older English, a person who listens to a speaker or to a reading
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语里，指听人讲话或听朗读的人
senses.example: The old sermon warned the auditor to remember what he heard.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧布道文告诫听者要记住所听的内容。
senses.why: This is the untouched Latin meaning, kept in writing long after the accounting sense took over.
senses.whyCN: 这是未经引申的拉丁语本义，在「查账」义占主导之后仍留在书面语中。

senses.title: The audit firm as one body
senses.definition: the firm or office that carries out an audit, referred to as a single actor
senses.definitionCN: 执行审计的事务所或部门，被当作一个行为主体来指称
senses.example: The auditor must be independent of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 审计方必须独立于被审计公司。
senses.why: Institutional language lets one noun stand for a whole team, so the word can mean the firm rather than one person.
senses.whyCN: 机构性语言允许一个名词代表整个团队，于是这个词可以指事务所而不是某一个人。

intro.en: Auditor is the agent noun of the Latin hearing family: the one who hears, first in a hall, later over a ledger.
intro.cn: auditor 是拉丁语「听」词族的施动者名词：听的那个人，先在厅堂里听，后来在账本上听。

items.en: The Latin verb for hear is generally linked to a root meaning to perceive; the reconstructed compound is disputed in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语表示「听」的动词一般被认为与「感知」词根有关；重构的复合形式在细节上有争议。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and its participle stem audit- was the base for agent nouns.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 是指人名词的构词基础。

items.en: Auditor meant a hearer or listener, and in Roman administration an official who heard accounts and claims.
items.cn: auditor 意为「听者」，在罗马行政中也指听取账目与申诉的官员。

items.en: Medieval courts and monasteries appointed auditors to hear accounts read aloud and to question the steward.
items.cn: 中世纪的宫廷与修道院指派专人听账，并向管家提出质询。

items.en: English took the word in the late fourteenth century for an examiner of accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪晚期借入这个词，指查账的人。

items.en: Nineteenth-century American colleges used the word for a student who only listens, reviving the plain Latin sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国高校用这个词指只听课的学生，复活了拉丁语的朴素本义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the hearing family with one false friend; the near-meaning group separates financial jobs by what they actually do.
note.cn: 形近组是「听」词族加一个假朋友；近义组按实际工作内容区分各种财务岗位。

entries.definition: the examination itself
entries.definitionCN: 审计这件事；同根的基础词。

entries.definition: relating to hearing
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；同根形容词。

entries.definition: the place where people hear
entries.definitionCN: 听的场所；礼堂，同根。

entries.definition: bold, daring
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；只是形近，词源与「听」无关。

entries.definition: a person who keeps or inspects financial records
entries.definitionCN: 会计；做账或查账的人，但不一定出具独立意见。

entries.definition: an official who checks that rules are followed
entries.definitionCN: 检查员；侧重实地查看，范围更宽。

entries.definition: a person who judges value or quality
entries.definitionCN: 评估员；侧重估价或评级。

entries.definition: a person who records daily transactions
entries.definitionCN: 记账员；只记录流水，不做独立核查。

normalIntro.en: Auditor is audit plus the agent ending -or: the person who does the hearing.
normalIntro.cn: auditor 就是 audit 加指人词尾 -or：做那场「听审」的人。

normal.en: The ending -or marks a doer, as in actor and doctor.
normal.cn: 词尾 -or 表示做事的人，如演员与医生。

normal.en: An external auditor comes from outside the firm.
normal.cn: 外部审计师来自公司之外。

normal.en: An internal auditor works inside the organization.
normal.cn: 内部审计员在机构内部工作。

normal.en: On campus an auditor listens but earns no credit.
normal.cn: 在校园里旁听生只听课、不拿学分。

normal.en: Auditor and auditory share the stem, not the meaning.
normal.cn: auditor 与 auditory 共用词干，意思却不同。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger with a pencil opposite the ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人拿着铅笔坐在账本对面。

abstract.en: Picture a tick appearing beside every second line.
abstract.cn: 想象每隔一行就出现一个钩。

abstract.en: Picture a back-row student with no exam paper.
abstract.cn: 想象后排一个没有试卷的学生。

examples.en: The auditor asked for the original invoices.
examples.cn: 审计师索要原始发票。

examples.en: Two auditors spent a week in the warehouse.
examples.cn: 两名审计师在仓库待了一周。

examples.en: He enrolled as an auditor and sat through every lecture.
examples.cn: 他以旁听生身份注册，听完了每一节课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥迪特」——开车来查账的那个人就是审计师；坐在后排只听课不考试的，也叫这个名字。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- 加指人词尾 -or，构成 auditor「听者」；因中世纪账目需口头宣读核对，转为查账人，十九世纪美国高校又用它指旁听生。

sensesIntro.en: One who hears: first a listener in a hall, then a checker of accounts and rules, then a student who only listens, and finally the firm itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「听的人」：先是厅堂里的听者，再是账目与规则的核查者，然后是只听课的学生，最后还可以指事务所本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outsider sitting opposite the ledger, listening and ticking
core.cn: 核心意象：外人坐在账本对面，边听边打钩

branches.en: a professional signing the report
branches.cn: 签署报告的专业人士

branches.en: a checker of rules and systems

branches.en: a student in the back row

intro.cn: 指人词尾 -or 把「听」的词干变成人；同一词干还造出行为、场所与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin auditor, a hearer, stands beside auditus, auditorium and audientia in the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auditor「听者」与 auditus、auditorium、audientia 同属一族。

latinEntries.example: Latin auditor already meant an official listener.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语里这个词已指官方听审者。

definition_zh: 有助于……的；促成……的；有利的
definition_en: tending to help bring about a result or to make a condition favourable
core_image: 一扇窗被推开一条缝，风顺着进来，桌上的火苗因此烧得更稳
scene: 图书馆把灯调到柔和，桌上只留一盏小台灯，翻书声几乎听不见。 A quiet room is conducive to concentrated work.
sceneCN: 这里 conducive 指某种条件有助于产生专注工作这一结果（第 1 个义项：有助于某结果）；句意为安静的房间有助于集中精力工作。

pos.zh: 有助于……的；促成……的；有利的

derivatives.zh: 有助于；促成
助益性
有助于地

senses.title: Helping bring about a result
senses.definition: tending to make a particular result more likely or easier
senses.definitionCN: 使某个特定结果更可能出现或更容易实现
senses.example: A quiet room is conducive to concentrated work.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的房间有助于集中精力工作。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to lead together': conditions walk beside a result and help it arrive.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「共同引导」：条件伴随结果同行，帮助它抵达。

senses.title: A favourable setting
senses.definition: of a place or atmosphere, favourable to a stated activity
senses.definitionCN: 指场所或氛围对某项活动有利
senses.example: The new studio is conducive to collaboration.
senses.exampleCN: 新的工作室有利于协作。
senses.why: A setting is not the work itself, but it can remove friction, and removing friction is what 'conducive' praises.
senses.whyCN: 环境本身不是工作，但它可以消除摩擦，而消除摩擦正是 conducive 所称赞的。

senses.title: Good for health
senses.definition: of conditions, helping the body stay well
senses.definitionCN: 指条件有助于身体保持健康
senses.example: Dry air and long walks are conducive to health.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的空气与长距离散步有益健康。
senses.why: The body responds to conditions before it responds to intentions, so the weather and the walking path are part of the treatment.
senses.whyCN: 身体先对条件作出反应，再对意图作出反应，因此天气与步行的路径也是治疗的一部分。

senses.title: Supporting learning
senses.definition: of arrangements, making learning easier or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 指安排使学习更容易或更有效
senses.example: Small classes are conducive to discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 小班教学有利于讨论。
senses.why: Learning needs room for a voice to be heard and answered, and a small class supplies that room.
senses.whyCN: 学习需要有让声音被听见并获得回应的空间，小班正好提供这个空间。

senses.title: Likely to cause error
senses.definition: of conditions, making mistakes more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指条件使错误更可能发生
senses.example: Too little sleep is conducive to error.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足容易导致出错。
senses.why: The word is neutral about the outcome: the same machinery that helps a good result can help a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对结果本身是中性的：帮助好结果的同一套机制，也能帮助坏结果。

senses.title: Helping peace
senses.definition: of measures or attitudes, making peace more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指措施或态度使和平更可能
senses.example: Open trade routes were conducive to peace.
senses.exampleCN: 开放的贸易路线有助于和平。
senses.why: Contact between groups gives each side something to lose, and that shared stake makes war less attractive.
senses.whyCN: 群体间的往来让每一方都有可失去之物，这份共同利害使战争不那么有吸引力。

senses.title: Suited to a purpose
senses.definition: of an arrangement, well suited to the end it is meant to serve
senses.definitionCN: 指安排很适合它所要服务的目的
senses.example: The seating plan was conducive to a short ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的座位安排适合一场简短的仪式。
senses.why: Every plan has a clock and a shape; arrangement is the part that lets the clock run without obstruction.
senses.whyCN: 每个计划都有自己的时钟与形状；安排就是让时钟不受阻碍地运行的那一部分。

senses.title: Allowing a process to run
senses.definition: of scientific or technical conditions, permitting a process to occur
senses.definitionCN: 指科学或技术条件允许某个过程发生
senses.example: Constant temperature is conducive to crystal growth.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温有利于晶体生长。
senses.why: A process needs its conditions held steady; when the surroundings stop interfering, the process can proceed on its own.
senses.whyCN: 过程需要条件保持稳定；当周围停止干扰，过程便能自行推进。

intro.en: Conducive comes from a Latin verb meaning to lead together, the same root as conduct.
intro.cn: conducive 来自一个意为「共同引导」的拉丁动词，与 conduct 同根。

items.en: English formed conducive in the 19c. from the verb conduce, originally in the sense of contributing to a result.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪由动词 conduce 造出 conducive，原义是「对结果有贡献」。

items.en: Conducere meant 'to lead together, bring along, contribute', from com- 'together' and ducere 'to lead'.
items.cn: conducere 意为「共同引导、带来、促成」，由 com-「一起」与 ducere「引导」构成。

items.en: Ducere 'to lead' gives conduct, duct, deduce and educate, all built on the image of a path being led.
items.cn: ducere「引导」产生 conduct、duct、deduce 与 educate，都建立在「引路」的意象上。

items.en: The fixed pattern 'conducive to' became standard in the 20c., especially in medicine, education and social science.
items.cn: 固定搭配 conducive to 在二十世纪成为标准用法，尤其在医学、教育与社会科学的文本中。

items.en: The word now covers settings, habits and policies, anywhere conditions can help an outcome along.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖环境、习惯与政策，凡条件能推动结果之处都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the leading root or looks similar; the near-meaning group names ways of helping a result.
note.cn: 形近组共享「引导」词根或拼写相近；近义组列出帮助结果发生的各种方式。

entries.definition: able to carry heat or electricity, a different notion.

entries.definition: to lead or guide, or the way something is carried out.

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「条件与结果同行」的画面留住。

normal.en: con means together, ducere means lead: conducive conditions lead a result along.
normal.cn: con 意为一起，ducere 意为引导：有利条件把结果一路带出来。

normal.en: Picture a window opened a little and a flame that burns better for it.
normal.cn: 想象窗户开了一条缝，火苗因此烧得更好。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is conducive to, so always ask 'to what?'
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 conducive to，所以要问「对什么有利」。

normal.en: Say con-DU-sive, with the leading root in the middle.
normal.cn: 读成 con-DU-sive，中间正是「引导」词根。

normal.en: Link it with conduct: both words lead something along a path.
normal.cn: 把它和 conduct 联系：两个词都把某物沿着路径引导。

abstract.en: The word is neutral about the end: it can help a good result or a mistake.
abstract.cn: 这个词对终点是中性的：它可以帮助好结果，也可以帮助错误。

abstract.en: A setting is not the work, but it can take the friction out of the work.
abstract.cn: 环境不是工作本身，但它可以去掉工作中的摩擦。

abstract.en: Conditions lead results the way a channel leads water.
abstract.cn: 条件引导结果，就像渠道引导水流。

examples.en: A quiet room is conducive to concentrated work.
examples.cn: 安静的房间有助于集中精力工作。

examples.en: The new studio is conducive to collaboration.
examples.cn: 新的工作室有利于协作。

examples.en: Too little sleep is conducive to error.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足容易导致出错。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（一起）+ duc（引导）+ ive：把结果一路带出来的条件，就是「有助于……的」。

root: 拉丁语 conducere（共同引导）：com-（一起）+ ducere（引导）

sensesIntro.en: Conducive always describes conditions that help a result along; the senses differ in the result, whether work, health, learning, peace or an error.
sensesIntro.cn: conducive 始终描述推动结果的条件；各义项的差别在于结果是什么，是工作、健康、学习、和平还是错误。

core.en: CONDITIONS LEAD A RESULT
core.cn: 条件引导结果

branches.en: Work and learning made easier by arrangement.
branches.cn: 通过安排使工作与学习更容易。

branches.en: Settings and plans suited to a stated purpose.
branches.cn: 适合特定目的的环境与安排。

branches.en: Health and peace helped by conditions.
branches.cn: 由条件促成的健康与和平。

branches.en: The negative case, where the same help produces error.
branches.cn: 负面情形，同样的助力产生错误。

branches.en: Technical conditions that let a process run.
branches.cn: 使过程得以运行的技术条件。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English adjective ending; its family is the family of leading.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语形容词词尾；它的同族词属于「引导」家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show conditions being led alongside a result.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示条件如何被引导到结果旁边。

items.example: The climate is conducive to trade.
They measured the conduciveness of the room.
items.exampleCN: 他们衡量了房间的助益性。

items.meaning: to lead out, hence to teach

derivatives.zh: 有助于
助益性
有助于地
